## Bomber batch A identities (BMB-A1, 2026-11-15)

Implementation, batch slice BMB-A1, Claude Sonnet. The three source reviews above
(B52-0, B2-0 and F117-0, all 2026-11-15) are now identities. `AircraftId` gains
`B52`, `B2` and `F117`, appended in that order after `Mf1`: `ALL` goes from 45 to 48
retail identities and `SELECTABLE` from 47 to 50 entries. The order is append-only
(batch rule B4): the Tornado IDS (Clean) that TOR-13 inserted into `SELECTABLE`
stays where it is (checkpoint code 46, wire position 45), so no existing code or
wire position moves.

| Checkpoint code | 47 | 48 | 49 |
| Wire position (place in `SELECTABLE`, 9 bits) | 47 | 48 | 49 |
| Place in `ALL` | 45 | 46 | 47 |
| `typeSize` | **612 (new arm**, the AC-130's) | 660 (explicit arm) | **588 (new arm**, the MiG-31's) |
| Short / long name | `B-52` / `B-52 Stratofortress` | `B-2` / `B- 2 Spirit` | `F-117` / `F-117A Nighthawk` |
| Shape stem | `B52` | `B2` | `F117` |
| HUD | `BMBROH.HUD` (the record's) | `B2.HUD` (explicit arm: the record's `hudName` is null) | `F117.HUD` (explicit arm: null in the record) |
| Cockpit stem / picture | `AC130` / `~AC130H.PIC` | `B2` / `~B2H.PIC` | `F117` / `~F117H.PIC` |
| PTS companion | none | `B2.PTS` | `F117.PTS` |
| Radar / gun | `B52R.SEE` / `M61.JT` | `F18R.SEE` / none | none / none |
| Live-fire default stores | `M61`, `AGM84E` | `MK82`, `PAVEWA3` | `PAVEWA3` |
| Strike class (rule, no override) | Heavy | Heavy | Attack |
| Interim rig: CODE bytes / runtime faces | 27,204 / 271 | 21,668 / 268 | 15,470 / 207 |
| State words | `7a20 7a26 7a2c 7a32 7a38` | `6486 648c 6498` | `4c56 4c5c` |
| Gear word / faces added | `7a26` +32 | `648c` +14 | `4c5c` +31 |
| Gear low point (shape units) | 14 at 2/3 ft | 33 at 1/3 ft | 21 at 1/3 ft |
| Draw scale | **2/3 ft a unit (header scale 2)** | 1/3 ft a unit | 1/3 ft a unit (identity; F117-2 owns the per-axis fit) |

**No record correction is applied.** Every record value is the retail value; the
corrections John accepted (decisions 5, 16, 23 and the rest) come in BMB-A2. The
wire identity is 9 bits since protocol 83, so 50 selectable identities use codes
0 to 49 of 512 and the compile-time assertion still passes; appending three
identities at the end needs no protocol change.

**John's accepted bindings applied (2026-11-15).**

| Decision | Applied |

| 14 (B-52 HUD) | Follows the record: `BMBROH.HUD`, the AC-130 panel family (`~AC130H.PIC`, `~AC130_P.PIC`). Bound by name; `AC130.PT` is not aliased. |
| 13 (B-52 gun) | `M61.JT` stays the B-52's gun and is a live-fire default; the move to the tail cone and the 1,242 rounds are BMB-A2 and B52-2. |

| Strike class | B-52 and B-2 sort Heavy by the rule (488,000 and 400,000 lb). |

**Interim choices (agent decisions 2026-11-15, until the cockpit and rig slices).**

| Choice | Interim | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HUD glass of the B-2 and F-117 | `hud_aperture.rs` fails closed (an empty mask) | `~B2H.PIC` and `~F117H.PIC` have no measured polygon. Their cockpit slices measure them. |
| (Update, F117-7, 2026-11-15) | The F-117's glass is measured (B2-7 did the B-2's) | See [F-117 ordnance, sensors and cockpit](#f-117-ordnance-sensors-and-cockpit-f117-67-2026-11-15). |
| HUD glass of the B-52 | The AC-130 family's whole-picture aperture (the arm the C-130, E-3, IL-76 and the airliners use) | The B-52 flies the same `~AC130H.PIC` picture, so it takes the shared reviewed glass; it needs no polygon of its own. Switch it to an empty mask if John wants it closed until a B-52 cockpit slice. |
| Rig | Gear word only; the other words pinned, unmapped | As batch 5: the shared fitted gear law until each aircraft's rig slice. |
| B-52 empty bay rows | Rows 5 and 6 keep an empty Mk 82 selection | The Harpoon and the M61 (the only defaults) fit neither row, so without a fallback the audit found the rows hiding compatible weapons (`live.rs`, the same device as the Mirage F1's belly pair). |

**The reader change (B2.SH loads).** `B2.SH`'s state guards use two conditional
jumps the reader refused with `unsupported shape state guard`: `0x7c` (jump if
less) and `0x7f` (jump if greater), both on the signed drag-rudder word `6498`.
`tore-formats/src/shape.rs` now takes them beside `0x74` (equal), `0x75` (not
equal) and `0x7d` (greater or equal): `0x7c` takes the branch when the word is
less than the immediate, `0x7f` when it is greater, signed. Decision 22 put this
in B2-2; the identity probe needed the shape to load. The reader still executes
no original code; it selects inert geometry. Tests: a unit test
(`signed_less_and_greater_guards_select_geometry_by_the_signed_compare`) covers
both opcodes against negative, zero and positive words and a non-zero immediate;
the existing flap-guard test now expects the next unknown opcode, `0x7e`, to be
refused (it had used `0x7f`); a retail-reading test (`bomber_batch_a.rs`) loads
`B2.SH` at 268 faces and checks word `6498` at 0, +1, -1 and 2 (268, 272, 272, 266)
and the gear word (+14).

*Retail-wide effect.* A scratch example (deleted afterwards) loaded every one of
the 1,275 shapes in `.local/m3-imports/scratch/shapes` through `Shape::parse`,
`Shape::with_export_state` and `Shape::scenery`, once with the reader before the
change and once after, and diffed the result lines (outcome, face, line and
billboard counts). **Exactly one line differs: `B2.SH`**, which goes from the
three `unsupported shape state guard` errors to 268 faces (269 in the export
state, 268 scenery). The other 1,274 shapes are identical, including the 17 that
already fail for reasons unrelated to guards (the effect and bullet pieces:
`BULLET`, `CHAFF`, `DEBRIS`, `EXP`, `F8`, `FIRE`, `FLARE`, `MOON`, `MOTH`,
`MOTHB`, `QUE`, `SMOKE`, `STARS`, `SUN`, `TRACER`, `WAVE1`, `WAVE2`). Nothing
else changes because the new arms only turn a former error into a branch.

**What the identity probe found.**

- The B-52's bay rows 5 and 6 (flags `0x1120`, no default store) need a retained
  selection, as above: with it the audit counts the two rows as recovered
  stations.
- The B-2's four bay rows carry flags `0x1504`, which include the decoded
  designator bit `0x400`, so the audit's designator-pod check (pins below) counts
  four pod placements on a B-2 that, on the real aircraft, has no pod station
  (B7). That is a retail row flag; BMB-A2 or the B-2 station slice decides it.
- The B-2 and F-117 cockpits have only the four panel pictures (`~B2.PIC`, `~B2H.PIC`,
  `~B2S.PIC`, `~B2_P.PIC` and the `~F117*.PIC` set), no left, centre or right
  overlay. `cockpit_overlays()` assumed overlays for any stem it did not list, so
  the first headless flight stopped at `aircraft cache missing ~B2_LH.PIC`;
  `B2` and `F117` now join the stems with no overlays (the B-52's `AC130` stem
  already was).
- `B52.PT` is the only one of the three without a `.PTS`, so `has_pts()` is false for
  it alone; `B2.PTS` and `F117.PTS` (inert) are expected.
- The F-117 record has no radar row (no `F18R.SEE`), so `radar()` is `None`; the
  B-2 keeps `F18R.SEE` (the B-1B's row, decision 18).
- The records are not parked targets and `parked_aircraft.rs` is unchanged.
- The deployed gear low point is 14 units at 2/3 ft for the B-52 (9.3 ft), 33
  units for the B-2 (11.0 ft) and 21 units for the F-117 (7.0 ft); real-size
  fits (F-117 per axis, F117-2) move them later.
  Update (F117-2, 2026-11-15): the F-117's low point is now 21 units times
  the height factor 0.8869, 18.62 units, 6.21 ft ([F-117 shape and real
  size](#f-117-shape-and-real-size-f117-2-2026-11-15)).
- The B-52's variety flight model takes the default ground alignment rate (0.7);
  the transport aircraft use 0.4. Flight tuning is B52-8's.

## B-52 shape, size and looks (B52-2, 2026-11-15)

Implementation, slice B52-2, Claude Sonnet. John's accepted decision 6 (2026-11-15:
draw at 2/3 ft per unit, lengthen the gear only if the frames show the belly or
pods too low) is confirmed in code and frames. BMB-A1 had already put the
B-52 at 2/3 ft a unit (`debris::scale`, the rig spec and the gear low point);
this slice measured every consumer and changed no production code. A retail-reading
test (`crates/tore-import/tests/b52_shape.rs`, skips without media) pins the numbers
and the `render-b52-skin` battery scenario draws the top and under views with the gear
down. Frames: `.local/m3-aircraft/frames/B52-2/` (local only).

**Size (spec-derived measurements, shape units at 2/3 ft).** `B52.SH` of `FA_2.LIB`
(CODE 27,204; the base archive is the only source). Neutral state: x -139 to 139, y
-138 to 107, z -9 to 42; gear word `7a26` adds 32 faces and the low point -14.

| Axis | Units | Feet at 2/3 | Real | Difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Span | 278 | 185.3 | 185 ft | +0.2% |
| Length | 245 | 163.3 | 159 ft 4 in (Jane's 160.9 ft) | +2.5% (+1.5%) |
| Height, gear down to fin tip | 56 | 37.3 | 40 ft 8 in | -8.2% |

**Gear and the decision (fitted measurements, agent decision, nothing lengthened).**

| Assembly | Faces | Measured (units, feet) |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Four tandem trucks | 6 each | centres y +39.5 and -31.5 (wheelbase 71 units, 47.3 ft); plates x 5 to 13 and -14 to -5 (about 12.3 ft between truck centres); z -14 to -6 |
| Two outriggers | 4 each | x +/-108 to 113 (74 ft out), y -38 to -32 (23 ft aft of the origin), z -14 to 3 (11.3 ft long) |

- Contact line: every truck and both outriggers reach z -14, which is 9.33 ft below
  the reference point; `models/variety.rs` uses the same 14 units at 2/3 ft. The
  outriggers touch the ground line with the wings at rest (the wing tip is at z 3,
  11.3 ft up, and the leg is 17 units). In the ground frames the truck wheels and an
  outrigger wheel sit on the runway.
- Clearance with the gear down: belly 3.3 ft (z -9), inboard pods 5.3 ft (z -6, x 45
  to 61), outboard pods 4.7 ft (z -7, x 79 to 96), drawn tank pods 7.3 ft, wing tip
  11.3 ft, fin tip 37.3 ft.
- **Decision: the gear stays as drawn.** The frames show a low, long-legged-looking
  bomber with the pods clear of the pavement; nothing reads as sunk or clipped. No
  published pod or belly clearance figure was found (a web search returned the layout
  only), so a lengthening of about 3.4 ft (5 units) to reach the real 40 ft 8 in
  would be a guess. It remains an option for John: lengthen all six assemblies by the
  same 5 units (fitted), which raises the belly to 6.7 ft and the pods to 8.0 and 8.6
  ft, and moves the variety gear low point to 19 units (12.7 ft). Not applied.

**Consumers at 2/3 ft.** The drawn aircraft, the stores preview and station
underside, the damage looks and their section extents, the damage bodies and pieces,
breakup offsets, the gear low point (9.33 ft) and the wingtip vapor point all use
2/3. The vapor record's points are +/-278 CE units, 92.67 ft out, exactly the drawn
tip (139 units), 2 ft up (the wing tip is at z 3) and 43.3 ft aft (inside the tip
chord); no fix needed. The generic rig scale equals `debris::scale` for the B-52 (a
test line was added beside the Tornado's). No consumer is still at 1/3.

**Not shape-derived (shared, unchanged, flagged).**

- *Hit volume.* One 28 ft sphere for every aircraft (`AIRCRAFT_RADIUS_FT`); the gun
  contact boxes are fractions of it (wings to 0.92, nose to 0.92, tail to -0.92). For
  the B-52 that is a hit box about 26 ft each side of the origin on a 92.7 ft
  half-span, 26 ft forward of the origin on a nose 71 ft out and 26 ft aft on a tail
  92 ft out: gunfire and fuzed weapons only touch the middle of the aircraft (the wing boxes reach 28 percent of the half-span). The transports
  (C-130, E-3) share this. A per-aircraft radius would change every aircraft, so it
  is John's call (flagged, not changed).
- *Eye point.* `mirrors::pilot_eye` is a fixed 10 ft forward and 7 ft up of the
  origin for every aircraft, and the front cockpit view sits at the origin. The B-52
  flight deck is drawn at y 88 to 100 (the windscreen, roof z 11), 59 to 67 ft
  forward and about 5 ft up: the rear view's seat is about 50 ft behind it. B52-7
  (cockpit) owns this.
- *Debris.* `debris::attachment` reads the shapes per axis at 2/3 with the identity
  per-axis factor; covered by the existing scale test.

**Skin.** 271 runtime faces (273 on the export path), one texture `_B52.PIC`. Twelve
exact-vertex twin groups, all with opposite stored normals (no MiG-21 exception, no
same-side sliver as the Tornado has); the smooth path pairs them and the top frame
shows no show-through. The wing tanks (x +/-113 to 117, at the wing tip) are drawn
airframe, no station (decision 10).

**Decals.** Two `E0` runtime decal slots on the export path, both 10 by 10 unit
plates one unit above the outer upper wing: slot 3 at `33b4` (left, x -126 to -136, y
-48 to -58, z 4) and slot 4 at `4676` (right). The runtime projector omits both and
the wing draws plain camouflage with no blank or skin-filled patch, as for the
Mirage 2000 and the Tornado. The nose art, fuselage codes and tail codes are textured
faces and draw whole; the fin carries no decal. No clipping and no fix needed.

**Damage looks.** `B52_A.SH` 372 faces, `B52_B.SH` 116, `B52_C.SH` 387, `B52_D.SH` 84
load at the intact shape's header scale (2). A is the body with the left wing cut at
x -43 (piece B is the cut-off section, authored about its own origin, x -71 to 62),
C the body with the right wing cut at x 82 (piece D, x -56 to 54, likewise); A and C lie inside the intact extents. No
whole-body variant is registered for the B-52 (`debris::damage_variant`), so a
destroyed B-52 draws the intact skin with regional cuts, as the Mirage 2000, the
Tornado and the MiG-25 do (open decision for John: registering `LeftWing` as variant
0 and `RightWing` as variant 1 would use the reviewed A to D pair, as the F-22 does
for the left wing). Frames at 0.6 and 1.0 (left-wing section, view 2 look 0,60, 120
ticks) show the wing cut at 1.0 with the fitted tear and fragment; the tail and core
sections at 1.0 also draw.

**A defect found on the way (not fixed, outside this slice).** With the B-52H the
game does not start in free flight or from a runway ground start: it stops with
"payload outside aircraft mass limits". BMB-A2 made the loadout cap the default tank
at 303,000 lb, but the flight state keeps the full 312,197 lb and
`flight::State::set_payload` rejects any payload on top of empty 185,000 plus that
tank (over 488,000 lb). Headless level flight does not call it, which is why BMB-A2's
checks passed. The frames and the battery scenario were captured with a temporary
local patch (`.local/m3-aircraft/checks/B52-2/set-payload-fuel-cap.diff`: when the
tank does not fit under the maximum, `set_payload` lowers it to what fits), reverted
afterwards. The patch is a proposal for the coordinator; without it
`render-b52-skin` fails at startup.

| Nose pair (two plates) | -6 to 7 | 71 and 97 | -24 and -14 | 8.0 and 4.7 |
| Nose strut and wheel | 0 | 88 to 96 | **-31** | 10.3 |
| Inner main plates | -65 and 62 | -2 to 20 | **-33** | 11.0 |
| Outer main plates | -71 and 69 | -7 to 41 | -27 | 9.0 |

The simulation's gear low point (`ground_clearance_ft`) is the inner mains, 33
units, 11.0 ft. The nose wheel therefore sits 2 units (0.67 ft) above the main
wheels when the aircraft is level, about 1.4 degrees of pitch over the 27.7 ft
wheelbase (nose strut y about 92, mains y about 9); the outer main plates hang
2 ft higher than the inner ones. The ground-start frames (`b2-ground-side`,
`b2-ground-side-zoom`, `b2-ground-front`, `crop3x-ground-gear`) show the mains on
the pavement and the nose wheel at or just above it, with no sinking or floating
that the eye can pick out. The belly clearance at the closed wells is 22 units
(7.3 ft).

### Drag-rudder poses (decision 22, checked)

The BMB-A1 reader fix is complete: word 6498 loads at every value, and the retail
test pins it.

| Value | Faces | Removed (closed pair) | Added | Look |
| ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 268 | none | none | both closed (neutral) |
| +1 | 272 | `465f`, `4679` (right) | six: upper plates `47db` and `47f5`, lower plates `47a7` and `47c1`, front plate `480f`, inboard cap `4829` | right rudder open |
| -1 | 272 | `4600`, `461a` (left) | six: `46d0`, `46ea`, `4704`, `471e`, `4738`, `4752` | left rudder open |
| 2 (and any larger) | 266 | `465f`, `4679` (right) | none | right pair removed, hole |
| -2 (and any smaller) | 266 | `4600`, `461a` (left) | none | left pair removed, hole |

Added geometry, raw units: right x 167 to 215, y -77 to -46, z -14 to 7; left x
-218 to -169, y -78 to -46, z -14 to 8. The two sides mirror about the mesh axis
(x = -1) within 1.5 units. Every added face is a whole quad, except the inboard

value 2 only): the second is the left-hand counterpart. The bay word 6486 adds
eight faces (four plates, two windings) and composes with the gear and rudder
words (`6486`+`648c`+`6498`=+1 gives 268 + 8 + 14 + 4).

The interim rig does not map the word (that is B2-3), so the poses were drawn
with a temporary, uncommitted, env-gated patch to `variety_animation.rs` that

`rudder-{0,1,m1,2}-top`, `-rear` and `-rear-left` and the 4x crops
`crop4x-rudder-1-right` and `crop4x-rudder-m1-left`: in the open poses a dark upper
plate and a lighter lower plate hang off the trailing edge outboard of the engine
bays, the right in +1 and the left in -1; pose 2 leaves an empty notch where the
right closed wedge was. No wrong winding, no missing faces and no show-through
anywhere in the four poses (the plates are drawn in both windings). The sign
convention (positive rudder opens the right, as the reader reads it) is B2-3's to
tie to the rudder input.

### Skin and decals

- **Twins.** 11 exact-vertex twin groups, all double-sided panels with opposite
  stored normals, so the smooth path pairs and hides the rear members and no
  MiG-21 exception is needed (retail test).
- **Decal slot.** The export path finds one `E0` slot the runtime path omits (269
  against 268 faces): address `2a73`, texture `@indexed:2`, a 7 by 5 unit plate
  (x 21 to 28, y 60 to 65, z 4 to 5) on the top skin right of the cockpit.
  It stays omitted, as on the Mirage 2000, the F-5E and the Tornado: the top view
  (`crop3x-nose-cockpit-top`) shows no blank or skin-filled patch, and the
  cockpit-side markings, the serial `USAF 21066` and the star-and-bar on the right
  wing are textured faces that draw whole. The top and under frames (gear down,
  `b2-top-view`, `b2-under-view`, and `render-b2-skin`) show no underside through
  the top skin and no z-fighting; the under view is the dark underside
  texture with the two gear-well panels and the bay panels.
- **Clipping.** None found: the open-bay plates, gear plates and drag rudders are
  separate whole faces, and the aircraft is a thin wedge with no part that crosses
  another.

### Damage looks

`B2_A.SH` 248, `B2_B.SH` 114, `B2_C.SH` 254 and `B2_D.SH` 74 faces load at the intact
header scale; `DamageArt::load` takes them with no error. Extents (raw units):
A x -237 to 95 (the right outer wing is gone), C x -259 to 257 with the nose 7 units
(2.3 ft) longer than the intact one (y 114 against 107), B x -62 to 158 and D x
-56 to 37 (pieces, smaller than the aircraft). No whole-body variant is registered
(`damage_variant`) for the B-2, so a destroyed aircraft draws the intact skin with
the regional cuts, as the other aircraft (damage 1.0 left-wing section: the left wing
cut, `b2-damage-1.0`). The two body variants
(`b2-damage-1.0-nose-variant` the A body; `b2-damage-1.0-tail-variant` the C body)
and 0.6 (`b2-damage-0.6`) all draw whole; the C body shows the interior, as the
other aircraft's C bodies do. The regional cuts follow the drawn extents (the wing
sections start at 30 percent of the half span), so on the B-2 they act on the whole
visible wing, not on the 26 ft the contact volume covers.

### Hit and damage volumes at true size (finding, nothing changed)

The sim's aircraft contact volume is not derived from the shape: the damage
sections are boxes in units of one 28 ft radius about the model origin
(`aircraft_contact`, `AIRCRAFT_RADIUS_FT`). In feet at 28 ft: core x +-7.8 and
10.6 aft to 5.0 forward; cockpit x +-6.2; nose x +-9.0, 11.8 to 25.8 forward; each
wing x 7.0 to 25.8 out, 7.8 aft to 10.6 forward; tail 25.8 to 9.5 aft. The B-2 is 86 ft to a
wing tip, 35.7 ft to the nose and 29 ft aft to the trailing edge, so **gun and
fragment contact covers only the inner 30 percent of each wing** (to 25.8 ft of 86)
and none of the outer wings, and the nose tip beyond 25.8 ft is outside. A round
that strikes the outer 60 ft of a wing misses; the same is true of a missile fuze,
which reads the same sphere. The regional damage looks and sections (above) are
shape-relative and so cover the whole wing. The same
fixed sphere applies to the B-52 (192 ft span) and the transports, so it is the
shared rule, not a B-2 error; making it per-aircraft (a radius or a box table keyed
by `AircraftId`) changes the simulation for the aircraft it touches (determinism,
`SIMULATION_VERSION`) and is John's decision, not made here.

### Eye point (finding, nothing changed)

The fixed seat is 7 ft up and 10 ft ahead of the model origin, that is shape y 30
and z 21. The B-2's own geometry there: the dorsal spine reaches z 24 (8.0 ft) at
y 40 (13.3 ft ahead), and the glasshouse is further forward (canopy top z 22, 7.3
ft up, y 60 to 70 and falling to z 14 by y 80: 20 to 27 ft ahead). The fixed eye
therefore sits 10 to 17 ft behind the glass and just under the spine skin. As on
the Mirage 2000, the F-15E and the Gripen the cockpit view draws the 2D cockpit
picture and takes no per-aircraft eye, so this does not show; B2-7 owns the cockpit.

Animation probe: `source_units_to_feet` 0.33333334 for the B-2; the four
required failures are the unmapped elevator, rudder, aileron and flaps (B2-3).

Frames (`.local/m3-aircraft/frames/B2-2/`, `.png` with `.ppm`; `cap.sh` and
`capg.sh` record the command: view 1 chase, 200 kt, `--instrument-layout small`,
1280x720, through `tools/agent-run.sh`): `b2-top-view`, `b2-side-view`,
`b2-front-view`, `b2-under-view`, `b2-threequarter`; ground `b2-ground-side`,
`b2-ground-side-zoom`, `b2-ground-front`, `crop3x-ground-gear`; drag rudders
`rudder-{0,1,m1,2}-{top,rear,rear-left}` and the crops; `crop3x-nose-cockpit-top`;
damage `b2-damage-0.6`, `b2-damage-1.0`, `b2-damage-1.0-nose-variant`,
`b2-damage-1.0-tail-variant`.

## F-117 shape and real size (F117-2, 2026-11-15)

Implementation, slice F117-2 of bomber batch A (worktree `m3-f117`, plan
`.local/m3-aircraft/PLAN-F117.md`). It mirrors M2K-2 (Mirage 2000, per-axis scale)
and TOR-2 (Tornado). The per-aircraft scale mechanism is the one M2K-2 built
([Aircraft shape scale](objects-and-shapes.md#aircraft-shape-scale-2026-11-09));
this slice adds the F-117 row to it. Nothing new in the mechanism.

**Decision.** John, 2026-11-15 (decision 24, "accept all"): scale the F-117 per
axis to its real size. **Opinionated (John, 2026-11-15); the factors are fitted
(agent derivation).**

**Re-measurement.** `f117.SH` with the gear word `4c5c` = 1, read with the shape
reader on 2026-11-15, 242 faces with the bay word as well, 238 with the gear
only: x -85 to 85 (170 units), y -96 to 93 (189 units: V-tail tips to the nose
probe tip; the probe is y 89 to 93), z -21 to 21 (42 units: gear low point to
fin tip; gear up the shape is z -6 to 21). At 1/3 ft a unit: 56.67 by 63.00 by
14.00 ft. This confirms the F117-0 extents exactly. The real aircraft is 43 ft
4 in span, 65 ft 11 in long and 12 ft 5 in high (FAS Military Aircraft F-117
page and Wikipedia, both read 2026-11-15; GlobalSecurity and the other
published pages agree; Airforce Technology and Fiddler's Green give the height
as 12 ft 9 in, 2.7 percent more, not used).

| Axis | Units | Raw ft | Real ft | Factor (`real * 3 / units`) | Scaled ft |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| x span | 170 | 56.67 | 43.33 | 0.76471, **0.7647** | 43.333 |
| y length (probe tip) | 189 | 63.00 | 65.92 | 1.04630, **1.0463** | 65.917 |
| z height (gear down) | 42 | 14.00 | 12.42 | 0.88690, **0.8869** | 12.417 |

The factors F117-0 proposed are right and are used as given: `[0.7647, 1.0463,
0.8869]` in `tore_formats::aircraft::scale::F117_SHAPE_SCALE`, one new arm in
`shape_axis_scale`. The length is matched to the shape's own extent including
the probe (the Mirage F1 rule); to the nose alone the factor would be 1.069.
Measured after scaling with the shape reader: 43.333, 65.917 and 12.417 ft.

**Leading-edge sweep.** The wing's leading edge runs from (13, 62) to (85, -71).
Measured from the lateral axis it is **61.6 degrees at identity and 68.4 degrees
after scaling** (the convex outline from the tip to the nose chine at (7, 80) gives
62.7 and 69.3). The real figure is about 67.5 degrees (67 degrees 30 minutes):
GlobalSecurity's F-117A specification page (reached through a web search; the
page itself answered 403 to a direct fetch) and f-117a.com's specification page
(its certificate had expired, so it was not fetched; the search snippet reads
67.30) give it. Wikipedia's text mentions a "high sweep angle (50 degrees)" without saying
what it is measured against, so it is not used. The scaled shape is within one
degree of the real sweep; the identity shape was 6 degrees short, which supports the
per-axis fit over uniform scaling (one factor cannot do 0.78, 0.96 and 0.89).

**What follows the scale.**

| Consumer | How | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Drawn shape, stores preview, parked draw, surface dump | every reader parses with `Shape::scaled(shape_axis_scale_f32(id))` | scaled, automatic |
| Rig | the interim rig (gear word only) parses the scaled shape at load; no hinge point is named (F117-3 and F117-4 must use `scale_point`) | scaled |
| Gear contact and low point | `variety.rs`: 21 units / 3 times the z factor | 7.00 ft becomes **6.21 ft**; wheelbase 18.3 to 19.2 ft, track 19.0 to 14.5 ft (the legs scale with the shape) |
| Station rows | `placed_scaled` with the right/up/forward factors | bay rows (4 and 5) x -/+10 units: **-/+2.55 ft** (was 3.33); up -22 units: **-6.50 ft** (was -7.33); forward -2 units: -0.70 ft (unchanged to 0.01 ft). The F117-0 proposal's mounts of +/-2.55 ft follow without a special arm. Fixed rows (0 to 3, jammer at -50 forward): 0 and -17.4 ft (was -16.7). F117-5 measures the bay on this geometry |
| Bay slot in the shape | the shape's open pose (word `4c56`) | 17.1 ft long, 1.0 ft wide, 2.4 ft deep (was 16.3, 1.3, 2.7) |
| Damage looks | `DamageArt::load` scales `F117.SH` and the A to D shapes alike; regional damage sections cut on the scaled extents | scaled, automatic |
| Debris attachment | `debris::attachment` scales the offset per axis | scaled (the F-117 has no registered damage variant, so the per-axis path is the same as the other variants' and has no direct F-117 test) |
| Wingtip vapor point | `streamer_world_points` with `right_up_forward` | on the scaled tip (the record gives (85, -5, -81) units, which scales to x 65.0) |
| Contrail and nozzle offsets | taken off the scaled shape; the shape has no flame word | follows; F117-4 maps the nozzle |
| Hit size | one 28 ft sphere for every aircraft (not shape-derived) | **not changed**, as in M2K-2. The real span is 43 ft, so the sphere is still generous; John's call whether a per-aircraft hit size is wanted |
| Pilot eye and cockpit camera | one fixed offset (7 ft up, 10 ft forward) for every aircraft (`mirrors::pilot_eye`) | **not changed**; the F-117's cockpit view and its glass aperture are F117-7's work |
| HUD | no HUD aperture (fails closed, BMB-A1) | nothing to scale yet |
| Parked placement | the F-117 is not a parked target (`parked_aircraft.rs` has no arm) | none |

Update (F117-4, 2026-11-15): the "F117-4 maps the nozzle" line in the table above did
not happen: the shape has no nozzle disc and no plume word, so no nozzle is mapped
and the contrail keeps its fallback attachment.

**Skin and decals.** 207 runtime faces (gear down 238; bay open 242), one
texture `_F117.PIC`. 19 exact-vertex twin groups, all pairs, **all with opposite
stored normals** (checked on the shape with a scratch program, not committed),
so no MiG-21-style exception is needed. Five `E0` decal slots (`161a` slot 4 on the
right wing underside at (57, -44), `2b91` slot 3 on the left wing top at (-56,
-41), `24c9` slot 1 and `251e` slot 0 on the two ruddervators, `2d44` slot 2 on
the fuselage side at x -7, y 27 to 34) are four-corner decal faces with an
indexed texture the runtime does not use; they stay omitted as in M2K-2 and TOR-2,
and the frames show plain skin in their place, no blank patch and no skin-filled
patch. Every other marking is a textured face and draws whole. The top and under
frames show no underside through the top and no z-fighting; the 3x crops of the
fin and the nose show no clipped marking. The new `render-f117-skin` scenario
pins this ([lane-flight](../testing/lane-flight.md)). No fix was needed.

**Damage looks.** `F117_A.SH` (233 faces), `F117_B.SH` (48), `F117_C.SH` (199) and
`F117_D.SH` (55) and their textures load through `DamageArt::load` at the same
scale (the frames at damage 0.6 and 1.0, left-wing and tail sections, draw the dark
patch, smoke and the regional cut on the scaled skin, with no loading error).
They are redrawn bodies and pieces, not copies of the intact faces (at most four
of A's 233 faces equal an intact face at any offset; A spans x -41 to 82 and C
x -84 to 85, so what each body leaves out was not identified here; the
F-5E's A and C are the nose and fin cuts). **No whole-body damage
variant is registered for the F-117** (`debris::damage_variant` returns none), so a
destroyed F-117 draws the intact skin with regional cuts, as the Mirage 2000,
Tornado, Gripen, MiG-25 and MiG-31 do; the F-5E registered A and C by agent
decision in F5E-2. Whether to register A and C for the F-117 is John's call
(open item 1 of the F117-2 log). The breakup pieces use the shared C body with the D
fragment at 1/3 ft a unit through `debris::variant`.

**Gear in the frames.** With the gear down on a runway (ground start at airfield
2, `ground-gear.png` and its 3x crop) the gear hangs under the belly at the
scaled size; contact is the 6.21 ft low point above, the same height factor as the
drawn legs, so the two agree by construction.

**Provenance.** Per-axis choice opinionated (John, 2026-11-15); factors fitted (F117-0
agent derivation, re-measured here); the 67.5 degree sweep and the dimensions are real figures
cited above; the omitted-decal, damage-variant, hit-size and eye-point choices are
agent decisions 2026-11-15, John's call to change.

## F-117 rig (F117-3, 2026-11-15)

Implementation, slices F117-3 and F117-4 of bomber batch A, run together (the shape
has only two state words). Worktree `m3-f117`, plan
`.local/m3-aircraft/PLAN-F117.md`. It mirrors the Mirage 2000 (M2K-3, M2K-4) and
Tornado (TOR-3, TOR-4) rigs: one own-source rig file,
`crates/tore-app/src/f117_animation.rs`, with its probe witnesses in
`crates/tore-app/src/aircraft_animation_probe/f117.rs`. The shape is already scaled
per axis (F117-2), so every hinge named below is a shape-unit point turned through
`scale_point` (F117-2 note), and a panel turned about it stays rigid in feet. The
fitted fit is also in [variety animation](../spec/variety-animation.md#f-117-rig-fit).

**Decision.** John, 2026-11-15, decision 27: rig the V-tail as whole ruddervators
with a small limit, mixing pitch and yaw as a V-tail does, and leave the elevons
unrigged. Opinionated (John, 2026-11-15); every number below is fitted (agent
decision 2026-11-15) unless it is marked as read from the shape.

### What is rigged and what is not

| Control | F-117 | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Elevator | rigged | collective ruddervator deflection |
| Rudder | rigged | differential ruddervator deflection |
| Aileron | **not rigged** | no elevon faces; probe records `not-applicable` and requires no motion |
| Flaps | **not rigged** | same (no flap faces) |
| Gear | rigged (F117-4) | three legs, three open-door plates, the door skins |
| Bay | rigged, **interim** (F117-4) | the shape's open pose, word `4c56`; F117-5 replaces it |
| Brake | none | no airbrake word, and the real jet has none; `not-applicable` |
| Exhaust and burner | wired, draws nothing | no afterburner, no plume word; `not-applicable` |
| Hook | none | the record has no hook |

Pitch and roll authority still come from the flight model; the missing elevons are a
drawing-only gap, as the F-15E's missing rudder was (the probe rule is the same:
`Expectation::Unsupported` for aileron and flaps, so the lever must move nothing).
The retail record has `afterburner thrust 0`, and `--flight-devices` already refuses a
nonzero fifth value for it; `flame()` is false and no nozzle faces are mapped
(`engine_material::outlet_count` stays 0), because the shape has no nozzle disc: the
real exhausts are slot exhausts and the aft body faces are plain skin. Nothing breaks:
the headless flight, the probe and the free-flight captures run as before, and the
contrail still takes the fallback attachment (15 percent of the span either side).

### Ruddervators (F117-3)

Each side is one assembly of 10 faces (right `22c5 22d9 231a 232e 2383 244b 2460 2475
24b3 2e40`, 36 vertices; left `23ab 23bd 23d0 23f7 240b 2425 2489 249e 24f6 255e`, 35)
that shares no vertex with any other face (F117-0). The rig refuses a shape in which
any face holds a vertex outside the reviewed 10-point set of its side.

- **Hinge (read from the shape, scaled).** Each assembly turns whole about its
  **root chord midpoint** on a **lateral cant axis**: the line from that midpoint to
  the tip chord midpoint, with no fore-aft part (rule 11: tilted by its own cant,
  never a swept span axis). Right: through (2, -67, 1), direction (21.5, 0, 20);
  left: through (-2.5, -67, 1), direction (-21, 0, 20). The cant measures 42.9
  degrees in shape units (right; 43.6 left) and 47.2 degrees on the scaled shape
  (right; 47.8 left); F117-0 gave "about 39 degrees" from a coarser reading.
- **Limit (fitted).** Each panel's trailing edge turns at most **0.15 rad (8.6
  degrees)** either way. **The real limit was not found** in any source read (a
  search for the F-117 ruddervator deflection returned only generic V-tail text);
  nothing is cited. For comparison the Tornado's tailerons take 0.25 rad and the
  fleet's tails 0.4: 0.15 is a small limit chosen so the root seam below stays small.
- **Mixing (fitted).** The angle that raises a trailing edge is `0.12 x elevator`
  (collective; a pull raises both) plus or minus `0.08 x rudder` (differential; a
  right pedal lowers the right panel's edge and raises the left's, which swings
  both trailing edges toward +X), the sum clamped to the 0.15 rad limit. Full pitch
  alone is 0.12 rad, full rudder alone 0.08 rad, both together reach the limit on
  one panel. Unit-tested and probe-witnessed in sign: a pull raises both trailing
  edges and moves them toward the centreline, a right pedal moves both toward +X.
- **Real layout note.** The real jet's ruddervators are usually described as hinged
  trailing-edge surfaces of the V-tail; the shape has no such faces, so the whole
  assembly turns instead (John's decision 27).

**Rule 11 fold table.** Right assembly: 10 faces, 3 or 4 vertices each, every vertex
turns, none stays fixed, none sits on the axis (the spindle passes through the panel
interior). Left: the same. No face folds. The probe measures the largest
inter-vertex distance change at 3.2e-6 ft over the 25-pose grid, `skin_gap_ft` 0.

**Root seam (measured, rule 11).** The assembly shares no vertex with the fuselage,
so the root is already 0.18 ft (right) and 0.15 ft (left) from the nearest fixed
face in the neutral pose, and a turn opens or buries it. The probe
(`seam-gap.csv`) follows the four root vertices of each side and reports the worst
one's distance to the nearest fixed triangle, and how far it travelled:

| Pose | Right gap, ft | Right root move, ft | Left gap, ft | Left root move, ft |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Neutral | 0.18 | 0 | 0.15 | 0 |
| Full pitch up (0.12 rad) | 0.39 | 0.51 | 0.29 | 0.51 |
| Full pitch down | 0.24 | 0.51 | 0.25 | 0.51 |
| Full yaw right (0.08 rad) | 0.19 | 0.34 | 0.26 | 0.34 |
| Full yaw left | 0.39 | 0.34 | 0.19 | 0.34 |
| Pitch up and yaw left (right panel at the 0.15 limit) | 0.36 | 0.63 | 0.23 | 0.17 |
| Pitch up and yaw right (left panel at the limit) | 0.25 | 0.17 | 0.31 | 0.63 |

Over the whole 25-pose grid the worst gap is **0.41 ft (right) and 0.31 ft (left)**,
and the largest root travel is 0.63 ft at the limit. About 0.2 ft of that is
the opening the turn adds; the rest is the gap the source already has. In the frames
the opening is a dark wedge beside the aft body, and at the limit it shows the
slot-exhaust grille texture through it. A fuller limit grows it with the angle (0.25
rad: 0.73 ft by the F117-3 pre-measure), which is why the limit is small. John's
call: accept it, or have the root hidden by a fitted fairing face.

### Gear (F117-4)

Word `4c5c` adds 31 faces (F117-0); the rig checks the exact set and each piece's
extent at load. They are flat plates in both windings, so the rig turns whole pieces:

| Piece | Faces | Vertices | On the hinge | Fixed off axis | Hinge (shape units) | Stow |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Right main leg (strut and wheel plates) | 6 | 24 | 2 | 0 | line along Y at x 30, z -4 (outboard top edge) | inward 90 degrees |
| Left main leg | 6 | 24 | 2 | 0 | line along Y at x -31, z -4 | inward 90 degrees |
| Nose leg | 6 | 24 | 0 | 0 | lateral line at y 36, z -5 (belly plane) | forward 90 degrees; steers first about the vertical line at y 40 |
| Right door (x 23 hexagon) | 2 | 12 | 4 | 0 | line along Y at x 23, z -4 | inward 90 degrees |
| Left door (x -25) | 2 | 12 | 4 | 0 | line along Y at x -25, z -4 | inward 90 degrees |
| Nose door (x 3 plate) | 2 | 10 | 4 | 0 | line along Y at x 3, z -4 | inward 90 degrees |
| Door skins (z -6, 7 faces) | 7 | 30 | 0 | 0 | lift 1.5 units (translation) | closed 0.5 units inside the belly |

No face folds. At gear 1 the pose is the source pose exactly and the lowest vertex is
**-18.62 units = 6.208 ft** (the F117-2 low point the flight model stands the jet
on, checked by the probe); gear 0 draws none of the 31. **Timing (fitted):** the
doors stay open while the legs swing, so the legs go from the source pose at gear 1
to stowed at gear 0.30 and the doors then close from 0.30 to 0, the skins lifting
with them; extension runs it backwards (doors open first, then the legs lower).
**Directions (fitted, no source found):** the mains retract inward and the nose
forward, hinges chosen so each stowed piece lies inside the skin; the real retraction
directions were not found. The nose hinge sits on the belly plane (z -5) instead of
its top edge (z -4) because at the top edge the strut's top corner stood 0.49 ft out
of the cockpit roof; at the belly plane it stands **0.24 ft** out (measured; the
probe gate is 0.3 ft). Every other stowed vertex is inside the neutral skin. The
doors and skins are interim: they ride the same schedule rather than a source
sequence, and F117-5's bay doors are separate work.

### Bay (interim, F117-4; F117-5 replaces it)

Word `4c56` swaps the belly triangle `34e6` for its other winding `351d` (a different
texture region: the belly painted open, with the two weapon trapezes) and adds the
two wall plates (`319c 31b1` at x -3, `31ff 3214` at x +1). The interim pose is the
shape's own: `state.bay` above 0 draws `351d` and the walls and hides `34e6`; each
wall (two windings) is one rigid plate that swings from flat inside the belly at bay
0.0 to the source pose at 1.0 about its top edge (z -4), outward. Left wall 6 vertices
a face, 4 of 12 on the hinge, 0 fixed. **It is minimal on purpose:** F117-5 cuts
two fitted belly bays with doors and the F-22 magazine mechanism, and this rig is
replaced then. `Flight::bay_available()` is true only for the F-22 family, so the
bay does not open in play yet (the probe and the stores preview set `state.bay`
directly); making it available belongs to F117-5 with the stations.
Update (F117-5, 2026-11-15): this interim pose is replaced by the fitted belly bays and
doors, and `bay_available()` is true for the F-117 ([F-117 weapon
bays](#f-117-weapon-bays-f117-5-2026-11-15)).

### Probe and checks

`--animation-probe` for `f117` (scope `reviewed-controls-and-attachments`): 207
neutral faces, **0 required/check failures**. Elevator, rudder, gear and bay
`required moved`; aileron, flaps, brake, hook and exhaust `not-applicable` (no
motion, as required); rotor and wing sweep stay `unreviewed` as for every fixed-wing
without them. The 25-pose pitch/yaw grid passes 25 of 25 (anchor not applicable,
skin gap 0, rigidity at most 3.2e-6 ft, direction witnesses 0); the 202-value dense
gear sweep passes every row (rigidity at most 1.9e-6 ft, hinge gap 0, skin gap 0,
ground contact at 1, stow overshoot at most 0.24 ft); the 8-value bay sweep passes
(rigidity at most 3.2e-7 ft, hinge gap 0). The battery animation lane registers
`f117` with those three sweeps (`dense-gear.csv` 203 lines,
`pitch-yaw-combinations.csv` 26, `bay-sweep.csv` 9) and the variety flight lane
registers it too (`flight-variety-f117`, 1,200 headless ticks).

**Frames** (`.local/m3-aircraft/frames/F117-3/`, png with ppm; `capture.sh`,
`batch-tail.sh` and `batch.sh` are the recorded commands). Ruddervators, rear
three-quarter (look 335,-12) and side (270,-5), zoom 3, gear and bay up: `tail-<pose>-rear`
and `tail-<pose>-side` for `neutral`, `pitch-up`, `pitch-down`, `yaw-right`,
`yaw-left`, `limit-right` (right panel at 0.15 rad) and `limit-left`; 4x and 3x
crops `tail-3x-<pose>-<view>` and the sheets `sheet-tail-rear`, `sheet-tail-side`;
the root seam close-ups `seam-8x-neutral-rear`, `seam-8x-pitch-up-rear`,
`seam-8x-limit-right-rear` and `sheet-seam-rear`. Gear, below (0,-60) and side
(270,-25): `gear-<down|mid|doors|near-up|up>-<below|side>` (gear 1, 0.5, 0.15, 0.03,
0) with `sheet-gear-below` and `sheet-gear-side`. Bay, through the GPU stores
preview cameras: `bay-<closed|half|open>-<under|oblique>` and `sheet-bay-oblique`.
I looked at the tail, seam, gear and bay frames: the panels turn whole, the wedge at
the root shows at the limit; the legs swing in and the doors close after them; the
open bay shows the painted trapezes between the walls. The views are oblique (the
orbit view does not hold the jet level) and carry the instrument windows.

**Provenance.** Faces and word roles spec-derived (retail shape, re-verified at
load); the cant axis and root midpoints read from the shape; ruddervator limit and
mixing, door timing, hinge heights, stow directions, the nose belly-plane hinge,
the skin lift, the 0.3 ft stow gate and the interim bay pose fitted (agent
decisions 2026-11-15); whole-assembly ruddervators and unrigged elevons per
decision 27 (John, 2026-11-15). Nothing attributed to John beyond that. No retail
bytes committed.

## Bomber batch A record and station corrections (BMB-A2, 2026-11-15)

Opinionated (John, 2026-11-15, "accept all" of the bomber decision round:
decisions 5, 13, 16, 23 and 26), implemented by slice BMB-A2. Earlier sections
above stay as written for the retail state; this one records what the game now
does. The behaviour and the sources of every changed number are in
[aircraft records](../spec/aircraft-records.md#bomber-batch-a-record-corrections-b-52h-b-2a-f-117a-bmb-a2-2026-11-15);
the audit pins in [ordnance availability](../baselines/ordnance-availability.md).

**Values (retail to game).**

| Aircraft | Field | Retail | Game |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| B-52H | Thrust, lbf / empty weight, lb / internal fuel, lb | 120,000 / 235,220 / 199,000 | 136,000 / 185,000 / 312,197 |
| B-52H | Fuel flow, lb/s | 18 | 20 (TF33-P-3 TSFC 0.52) |
| B-52H | Tail gun rounds (row 4) | 2,000 | 1,242 |
| B-2A | Thrust, lbf / empty weight, lb | 114,000 / 100,000 | 69,200 / 158,000 |
| B-2A | Internal fuel, lb / maximum take-off, lb | 180,000 / 400,000 | 167,000 / 376,000 |
| B-2A | Bay rows 5 to 8 flags | `0x1504` | `0x1104` |
| F-117A | Maximum take-off, lb / ceiling, ft | 54,000 / 42,000 | 52,500 / 45,000 |
| F-117A | 1 G fast edge at 36,000 ft, ft/s | 1,020 (Mach 1.05) | 891 (Mach 0.92) |
| F-117A | Row 2 default | `F18.ECM` | none |

**The F-117 envelope, point by point (speed ft/s at altitude ft).**

| Row | Retail | Game |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 G | 285@0, 305@17000, 367@30500, 458@37750, 570@42000, 715@42000, 847@40000, 1020@36000, 1000@0 | 285@0, 305@17000, 367@30500, 458@37750, 570@45000, 715@45000, 847@40000, 891@36000, 1000@0 |
| 0 G | 250@0, 265@16000, 327@29500, 418@38750, 570@44000, 715@44000, 897@42000, 1090@36000, 1060@0 | the same with the two top vertices at 47000 and 961@36000 |
| -1 G and 2 G | 315@0, 335@17000, 392@25500, 481@30750, 570@34000, 710@35000, 960@34000, 980@0 | 960@34000 becomes 897@34000 (held to the 1 G edge); the rest as retail |

No other row's vertex moves (every other fast side is already inside the new 1 G
edge). Guards: the corrections apply only while `maxAlt`, the 0 G and 1 G rows and the
station rows are the retail ones (`aircraft_corrections.rs`, `aircraft_stations.rs`).

**The B-52 fuel finding (the record validators).** Empty 185,000 plus fuel 312,197
is 497,197 lb, over the 488,000 lb maximum. The record validator (`Aircraft::parse`,
"aircraft empty plus fuel exceeds MTOW") and `Configuration::validate` rejected that
sum; both now reject only an empty weight at or above the maximum. TORE had no fuel
cap: `Loadout::new` filled the tank and the takeoff check refused an overweight load,
so the default B-52 load would have been refused. `Loadout::new` now caps the starting
tank so the default load fits (303,000 lb, whole pounds); no other aircraft is
touched. Free flight and `--headless-flight` use the model's full tank. Loadout
weight counts external stores only (`!s.internal`), so the B-52's and B-2's bay loads
(16,560 lb of Harpoons, up to about 50,000 lb at the row classes) are outside the
takeoff total.

**Station rows.** The B-52's tail gun row (4) takes 1,242 rounds; its position stays at
(0, 6.7, -73.3) ft (B52-5 moves it to the tail cone). The B-2's four bay rows lose the
designator bit, so pods and the several-projectile stores are no longer offered there
(weapon placements 102 to 86, pods 84 to 80). The F-117's row 2 keeps its place,
mask, count and position but no default store, which removes the late-Cold-War
jammer and 30 chaff and 30 flares of `F18.ECM`; no dispenser is added.

**Not corrected, listed for John.** B-2 fuel flow (6 lb/s, the B-1B's; the cited
F118-GE-100 TSFC 0.375 gives 7), F-117 fuel flow (2 lb/s, 0.333 implied; no cited
F404-F1D2 value found), the B-2 and B-52 top speeds and sea-level edges, the B-2
49,000 ft ceiling (real 50,000), and the engine count: `Configuration::from_source`
clamps `engines` to 1 to 4 (`live.rs`), so the B-52's eight engines read as four
(an existing behaviour, not touched here; B52-8's call).

## B-52 rig (B52-3, 2026-11-15)

Implementation, slices B52-3 and B52-4 run together (bomber batch A), Claude Sonnet
(sonnet-high). Binding: John's accepted decisions 11 (no drawn roll surface, the
stabilizer takes its real pitch range) and 12 (the outriggers retract with the gear,
no crosswind crab), 2026-11-15. The B-52 now loads through its own rig,
`crates/tore-app/src/b52_animation.rs` (the shared `variety_animation` row keeps only
the layout, the scale and `supported`), with its own probe module
(`aircraft_animation_probe/b52.rs`) and battery entries (`flight-animation-b52`).
Nothing in the simulation changed. Frames are local only, in
`.local/m3-aircraft/frames/B52-3/`.

Provenance: the face lists, hinge edges and gear plates are **spec-derived** (retail
`B52.SH`, read at load and refused if they differ). The stabilizer range and the
outrigger direction are cited real facts; everything that moves a piece (the limits that
no source gives, the hinge lines, the stow turns, the timing, the interim bay drop) is
**fitted**, agent decisions of 2026-11-15, labelled below. No retail bytes are committed.

### Word map (identified)

| Word | Faces | Reading | Rig |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `7a20` | +4 | Bay: two plates (x -7 and +7, y -13 to 26, z -13 to -8), both windings | Drawn while `state.bay` > 0, dropping from the belly line (interim, fitted) |
| `7a26` | +32 | Gear: four trucks (6 faces each) and two outriggers (4 each) | Appended to the shape, hidden at gear 0, six rigid assemblies |
| `7a2c` | -2 | Left flap word: deletes the left inboard wedge `4f3b 4f5a`, adds nothing | Pinned at load, never set |
| `7a32` | -2 | Right flap word: deletes `4e54 4e73`, adds nothing | Pinned at load, never set |
| `7a38` | +2 / -2 | Rudder word: swaps the full-height quad `50f0 5117` for a skewed copy `5016 503d` | Pinned at load, never set; its pose gives the travel |

The slot order of the flap words was "unconfirmed" in B52-0. `Shape::with_state` now
shows it: `7a2c` removes exactly the two left faces and `7a32` exactly the two right
faces, so the left and right reading is confirmed (the rig checks the exact removed
and added address sets for all five words and refuses a shape that differs). The rig
never sets the flap or rudder words: it keeps the neutral wedges and the neutral
rudder drawn and turns them whole, so the wing and the fin never show a hole.

### Rule 11 face table

| Surface | Faces | Vertices | Move | On the hinge | Fixed |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Stabilizer right | `334e 3361` (two windings) | 4 each | 4 | 0 | 0 (shares no vertex with any face) |
| Stabilizer left | `3167 317a` | 4 each | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| Flap wedge right | `4e54` (lower skin), `4e73` (upper skin) | 4 each, 6 distinct vertices | all | 0 (the hinge is the mid line of the thick leading edge) | 0 |
| Flap wedge left | `4f3b`, `4f5a` | 4 each | all | 0 | 0 |
| Rudder | `50f0 5117` (two windings) | 4 each | 2 | 2 (the forward edge, shared with the fixed fin faces `3396 3434`) | 0 |
| Truck (four) | 6 faces | 5 and 4 | all, one rigid piece | | 0 |
| Outrigger (two) | 4 faces (crossed plates) | 4 | all, one rigid piece | | 0 |
| Bay plates | `4dfb 4e12 4d5e 4d75` | 4 | 2 (the lower edge) | 2 (top edge on the belly line) | 0 |

No face has a vertex held fixed off its hinge, and no panel folds: every one turns as a
whole rigid piece (the probe measures the largest inter-vertex distance change at
zero feet).

### Stabilizer (decision 11)

Each side is one floating quad at z 5 that touches no other face, so a whole-panel
turn folds nothing and opens no seam (the probe's anchor gap is 0 ft). It turns about
a lateral X axis through the root chord midpoint, right (4.5, -100.5, 5) and left
(-4.5, -100.5, 5), the quad being flat so there is no anhedral to tilt the axis.

**Real range (cited).** "The stabilizer is adjustable through 13 degrees of movement
(nine up, four down)" (Wikipedia, "Boeing B-52 Stratofortress", Flight controls; the
page also says the stabilizer is crucial in takeoff and landing "due to large pitch
changes induced by flap application"). B52-0 had already quoted the 13 degrees. The
source does not say which end "up" means. **Fitted reading:** nine degrees of nose-up
trim (trailing edge up) and four of nose-down trim (trailing edge down), the larger
travel being the one the flaps need and the sense of a pull in the fleet. At 2/3 ft a
unit the aft tip corner (22.5 units from the spindle) moves 2.35 ft up at nine
degrees and 1.05 ft down at four; the leading root corner (19.5 units) moves 2.03 ft
the other way at nine.

**Choice (fitted): the drawn stabilizer is the pitch surface.** On the real jet the
stabilizer trims slowly and a separate elevator pitches the aircraft; the shape has no
elevator and the state carries no trim. So the one drawn pitch panel follows the
elevator command directly over the real trim range: a full pull raises the trailing
edge nine degrees, a full push lowers it four, and the travel is linear in between
(`0.5` gives 4.5 and 2). The alternative (a trim-only stabilizer driven by a slow trim
state with the elevator undrawn) would need new state; it is left to John.

**Roll (decision 11).** No drawn roll surface. The G and H have no ailerons and roll
with six spoilerons a wing that the shape does not draw. The probe marks the aileron
`Expectation::Unsupported` (the F-15E rudder and F-117 elevon precedent): the lever
moves nothing and the probe fails the run if it ever does.

### Flaps and the seam (rule 11 choice)

The two inboard strips (x 9 to 53, chord 8.2 units, 5.5 ft) are each a thin wedge:
two faces sharing the aft knife edge, the thick leading edge shared with fixed wing
faces along its whole length. They turn as one rigid wedge about the mid line of the
leading edge, right (15, 7, 8) to (53, -14, 6.5), left from (-53, -14, 6.5) to (-15, 7,
8) so that a positive angle lowers the trailing edge on both sides. The two leading
vertices at each end sit 2 and 1.5 units off the line, so the leading edge opens by at
most 4 sin(angle/2) units (0.52 units, 0.35 ft at the limit).

The trailing corners (9, 1, 9) and (47, -20, 7) (left (-9, 1, 9) and (-48, -20, 7)) are
shared with fixed faces (`2651 2664` at the root, `3d8b 3e29` at the outer end), 8.2
units from the line, so a turn opens a seam there of 2 x 8.2 x sin(angle/2) units. B52-0
measured the source's 2.7 ft at 30 degrees (5.5 ft x sin 30; the true chord gap is 2.8
ft). Options considered: a smaller limit, a different hinge, or a fitted fill face. A
hinge on the trailing edge only moves the problem to the whole leading edge, which is
shared with fixed faces along its length; a fill face would add new geometry the
source does not have. **Chosen (fitted): a smaller limit, 15 degrees (0.2618 rad)**,
about half of the real jet's large flap angle (no cited B-52 flap angle was found).
**Seam in the end state: 1.43 ft at the inboard trailing corner on each side (probe,
flaps 1.0; 0.72 ft at 0.5, 0.36 ft at 0.25) and 1.43 ft at the outboard corner (the
same distance from the hinge), in a 185 ft airframe; the strips are rigid to 0 ft.**
The inboard end sits against the fuselage side and the outboard end beside the
inboard engine pod. A fill face remains an option if John finds the crack
visible in the frames.

### Rudder

The full-height quad (z 11 to 42, chord about 8 units) turns about its own forward
edge, (0, -101, 11) to (0, -114, 42), the edge it shares with the fixed fin faces, so
nothing folds. **Travel is the retail word's pose (spec-derived):** the skewed copy in
`7a38` moves the top rear vertex 4 units (7.4 units from the hinge line) and the
bottom rear 8 units (14.8 units), a turn of 31.8 and 30.0 degrees about the hinge:
0.54 rad (30.9 degrees) on average, to +X only, so the rig turns the neutral quad by
0.54 rad x rudder (the load check refuses a word that differs by more than 0.06 rad).
The retail swap is a skew rather than an exact rotation (the radii differ by 3 and 8
percent), so a rigid turn reproduces it to within 0.4 units. The negative direction is
the mirror (fitted). At full travel the top rear vertex moves 2.53 ft out of the fin
plane and the bottom rear 5.06 ft. **No real B-52 rudder limit was found** (the
sources say only "a relatively small, narrow chord rudder", Wikipedia); the word's pose
is used instead, and 31 degrees is likely generous for the real jet.

### Gear and outriggers (decision 12)

All six assemblies are one gear word, `7a26`, appended to the shape and hidden at gear
0. All move together, linearly with the gear fraction (fitted timing: no stagger, no
doors, since none are drawn). No crosswind crab (decision 12). The real retraction
directions were **not found**: Jane's (`B52.INF`) has "four individually retracted
twin-wheel main units in tandem pairs" and "small outrigger units retract inward into
wings outboard of outer engine positions" (cited in B52-0); Wikipedia and the
Aviationist's gear article give the layout and the 20 degree crosswind steering but not
the direction. Hinges below are **fitted**.

- **Trucks (four).** Each truck (x 5 to 13, left -5 to -14, z -14 to -6) turns 90
  degrees as one piece about a line along Y on the keel at the belly edge, (0, y, -8),
  swinging up the fuselage side. A smaller turn about a hinge on the truck's own edge
  cannot work: the truck is 8 units wide and 8 high, wider than the section above the
  side wall allows. At stow every vertex of all four trucks lies inside the fuselage
  section (belly z -9, side x 8 from z -6 to 5, narrowing to the roof) with at least
  0.2 unit of margin (probe, near-stow sample, both sides; the left truck is one unit
  wider). The path only rises from the gear-down pose. The motion passes through the
  skin on the way (no doors drawn).
- **Outriggers (two).** Each outrigger (leg 17 units, crossed plates) turns 90 degrees
  inward about a line along Y at its own x (+/-111) and z 4.1, between the wing's
  lower skin (z 3.7) and its upper skin (4.5 to 5.8), so it ends lying along the
  wing, inboard of its wheel position (the real direction: inward into the wing,
  Jane's). The side plate (the x = +/-111 plane) lies flat at z 4.1 between the skins
  (probe check). **Limitation:** the cross plate is 5 units wide, thicker than the
  0.8 unit gap, so near stow it stands 3 units (2 ft) through the wing skins. Nothing
  rigid fits there; the outriggers are not drawn at gear 0, so only the last instant of
  the retraction shows it. The cross plate is also 2 units wider than the hinge, so it
  dips 0.11 unit (0.07 ft) below the ground contact line near the start of the turn.
- **Gear down** is the source pose: the lowest point is the contact line, z -14 (9.33
  ft), unchanged from B52-2.

### Brakes, burner and the engines

No airbrake is drawn (the real B-52 brakes with its spoilers, which the shape does not
show; Jane's lists a 44 ft ribbon braking parachute, not drawn), so the brake control
is `Expectation::Unsupported` (not applicable). The jet has no burner and the shape no
flame word: exhaust is not applicable too, and `flame()` is false. The engine
nozzles are not mapped: the transports (C-130, AC-130, E-3, Il-76, B747, A310) map
none (`engine_material::outlet_count` is 0 for them) and the nozzle glow supports
at most two outlets, the B-52 has eight. The contrail offsets fall back to the
bounds-based spread (flagged for John below).

### Interim open bay (word 7a20)

B52-5 replaces it with fitted belly bays and doors. Until then the two retail plates
(both windings) are drawn while the bay is open and drop out of the belly: the top
edge stays on the belly line (z -8) and the lower edge falls to z -8 - 5 x bay. This
is a presentation only (the same device as the B-2's interim plates); the lowest
point is 5 units (3.3 ft) under the belly, above the gear contact line.

### Probe and battery

`--animation-probe` on `b52`: 271 neutral faces, 0 required and check failures, scope
`reviewed-controls-and-attachments`. Elevator, rudder, gear, flaps and bay are
`required moved` (5, 5, 22, 5 and 5 distinct poses); aileron, brake, exhaust and hook
are `not-applicable` and stay still; the neutral pose equals the source. The b52
module restates the witnesses independently (rigid to 0 ft, the spindle and hinge
points stay at 0 ft, direction and magnitude of the stabilizer tip against the real
range, the rudder rear vertices against the word, trucks inside the section, the
outrigger side plates between the skins). Two combination files: a 25 pose pitch
against rudder grid (`pitch-yaw-combinations.csv`) and a 202 value dense gear sweep
(`dense-gear.csv`). The battery entry `flight-animation-b52` checks the two files'
row counts. One rig unit test (`b52_animation::tests`) covers the stabilizer limits,
the flap wedge and its seam, the rudder, the gear stow and the bay on synthetic faces.

### Frames (local only)

`.local/m3-aircraft/frames/B52-3/` (png with ppm; view 2, look yaw and pitch are orbit
angles, the aircraft is in free flight so the views are not exact orthographics; the

`rudder-top-3x-neg-0-pos` (the fin turns to either side of neutral). Stabilizer

### Open for John
