## B-52 flight review (B52-8, 2026-11-15)

Implementation mode. The B-52H flies the hybrid adapter's `variety` configuration built
from `B52.PT` with BMB-A2's real thrust (136,000 lbf), empty weight (185,000 lb), tank
(312,197 lb), flow (20 lb/s) and the record's own 488,000 lb maximum takeoff, G rows
(-2 to +3) and envelopes. None of those changed, nor did the top-speed edges. What
changed is the shared large-aircraft flight tuning, for this aircraft only, the way the
transports' 0.96 level-speed fraction and 0.4 nose alignment are per-aircraft (see
[variety flight](../spec/variety-flight.md#boeing-b-52h-b52-8-2026-11-15) and the
[variety flight baseline](../baselines/variety-flight.md#boeing-b-52h-validation-2026-11-15)).
Every term below is **fitted**, an agent decision of 2026-11-15; none is retail behaviour.

### Causes

1. **The drag law, not the thrust.** The hybrid drag equals the full thrust at the 1 G
   top-speed edge and falls with the square of the speed below it. That suits an
   aircraft whose edge is the thrust-limited top speed. The B-52's low-altitude edge
   (385 kt at sea level, 440 kt at 15,000 ft) is a placard, so at 300 kt the law gave
   about 0.6 of the full thrust as drag (about 80,000 lbf for a 400,000 lb aircraft whose
   real clean drag is about 28,000). Climbing, accelerating and range all suffered:
   2,100 ft/min up to 5,000 ft, 2,600 nautical miles at Mach 0.77.
2. **The turn "failure" is a probe point on the top-speed edge.** Mach 0.7 at 15,000 ft is
   439 kt and the record's 1 G edge there is 440 kt, so the probe's full-power turn had
   no thrust left by construction. A turn at a held speed is limited by the G rows, not
   by thrust: 42 degrees (1.35 G) at the edge and 54 to 60 degrees (1.7 to 2.0 G) at
   250 to 400 kt, before and after. The 1,000 ft instantaneous 1.22 G was at 461 kt, 20
   percent over the record's 385 kt sea-level edge (the fast-side hold gives the 2 G row
   divided by the 1.64 loading divisor); that is the record's, not changed.
3. **The probe's 450 kt climb start** was above the 385 kt sea-level edge: nothing
   climbed. The probe now takes `PROBE_CLIMB=bomber` (300 KCAS, then Mach 0.77, from
   250 kt, military power).
4. **Thrust at altitude.** The shared lapse (`exp(-h/70,000)`) keeps 0.6 of the sea-level
   thrust at 36,000 ft, where a TF33 keeps about 0.3.
5. **No takeoff drag and a stale approach weight.** The shared takeoff has no flap, gear
   or induced drag and no loss of thrust with speed, so the 488,000 lb run was 5,807 ft.
   And the scripted approach was built before `--flight-fuel` was applied (a general
   probe defect, fixed below), so every approach flew the weight of the full ground-start
   load.

### The fitted terms

| Term | Shared value | B-52H | Fitted against |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clean-drag shape (`DragShape`: 0.15 of the reference drag on the square law, the rest on the 12th power of speed over the edge) | square law | 0.15 / 12 | Published 6,270 ft/min climb and 442 kt cruise at about 7,600 nautical miles. 1 at the edge, so the top speed does not move. At 0.78 of the edge 0.13 of the thrust (about 18,000 lbf at sea level; a real clean 400,000 lb aircraft has about 28,000 there, the missing induced drag at low speed is not modelled), at 0.857 (Mach 0.77 at 36,000 ft) 0.24 |
| Thrust lapse height | 70,000 ft | 32,000 ft | TF33-P-3 keeps about 0.3 of its sea-level thrust at 36,000 ft and Mach 0.8 (0.32 here). The cruise burn is the throttle fraction, so this does not move it |
| Rolling and takeoff-run deceleration | 0.8 ft/s squared | 4.8 | A pilot forum estimate of about 8,000 ft ground run at 488,000 lb; carries flap, gear and induced drag and the thrust lost with speed, which the shared takeoff lacks. A hands-off unbraked rollout is therefore short; braked landings use the next row |
| Wheel brake deceleration | 18 ft/s squared | 2.6 | The same forum's 4,900 ft landing ground run from a 135 kt flare at 270,000 lb with brakes alone. 18 stopped a heavy from 140 kt in about 1,500 ft |
| Stall reference fraction | 1 | 1.09 | The reference weight of the weight-scaled stall is the empty weight times it. 135 kt flare at 270,000 lb is a flapped stall near 108 kt at 1.25 times; 1.09 puts the model there (it was 113 kt, and 152 kt at 488,000 lb, now 145) |
| Ground alignment rate | 0.7 | 0.4 | The transports' value (C-130, AC-130, E-3, IL-76, E-2); the precedent for a heavy. Was the fighters' default (BMB-A1 open item) |

Code: `crates/tore-sim/src/models/variety/b52.rs` (the terms and their notes),
`models/config.rs` (the optional `DragShape` on `Aerodynamics`, validated),
`flight/airframe.rs` (the one drag expression, `None` is the old square law),
`models/variety.rs` and `models/mod.rs` (the per-aircraft hooks). Every other aircraft
has `drag_shape` `None`, the shared lapse, rolling, brake, stall and alignment values;
one test checks that for every variety identity.

### Before, after and real

Weights: full tank is the free-flight and `--headless-flight` start (185,000 + 312,197 =
497,197 lb, over the 488,000 lb maximum), max is the Load Ordnance default (488,000 lb),
typical is 400,000 lb (fuel 215,000). Ground figures are the ground-start load at the
named weight on a 12,000 ft runway (Greece, airport 1) unless a column says otherwise.
Logs: `.local/m3-aircraft/checks/B52-8/{before,after}/`.

| Figure | Before | After | Real (source) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Takeoff ground run to liftoff, 488,000 lb | 5,807 ft (UKR 1) | 7,674 ft (UKR 1), 7,324 ft (GRE 1) | about 8,000 ft at 488,000 lb, 500 ft, 60 F, no wind (pilot forum estimate, unofficial); 9,843 ft takeoff distance (UltimateSpecs) |
| Liftoff speed, 488,000 lb | 162.5 kt | 158.6 kt | no primary figure; battery window 150 to 175 kt |
| Takeoff, 416,600 lb / 301,600 lb | not measured | 4,843 ft, 147.8 kt / 2,081 ft, 125.4 kt | none found |
| Climb, time to 5,000 / 36,000 / 50,000 ft (full / max / typical) | 143 / 1,151 / 1,712 s, 141 / 1,136 / 1,688 s, 127 / 987 / 1,355 s | 82 / 638 / 978 s, 81 / 630 / 964 s, 73 / 556 / 834 s | none found for times |
| Climb rate, 0 to 5,000 ft average (full / max / typical) | 2,100 / 2,130 / 2,360 ft/min | 3,660 / 3,700 / 4,110 ft/min (best 5 s: 5,075 / 5,120 / 5,590) | 6,270 ft/min (Wikipedia and UltimateSpecs, weight and altitude not stated) |
| Cruise, Mach 0.77 at 36,000 ft (441 kt), steady burn and range from 312,197 lb | 14.7 lb/s, 2,600 nautical miles | 4.7 lb/s, 8,200 nautical miles | cruise 442 kt; combat range about 7,600 nautical miles (8,800 miles), Wikipedia and the Air Force fact sheet |
| Level top speed at 36,000 ft | 514.9 kt | 515.3 kt | 560 kt (UltimateSpecs), 565 kt (Wikipedia, Mach 0.86); Jane's 516 kt (Mach 0.90) is the record's edge. Reported, not changed |
| Level top speed at sea level / 15,000 ft | 385 / 439 kt | 385 / 439 kt | none found (the record's edges are placards) |
| Ceiling | envelope top 55,000 ft; zoom to 50,600 to 53,200 ft | the same | 50,000 ft (Air Force, Wikipedia); Jane's 55,000 ft. The record's 55,000 is Jane's; reported, not changed |
| Approach, 270,000 lb | 166.2 kt (the 0.85 times landing-limit cap, flown at the full ground-start weight) | 140.3 kt, touchdown 131.6 kt, rollout 4,131 ft | 135 kt flare speed at 270,000 lb; 4,900 ft ground run without a chute (pilot forum) |
| Approach, 404,000 lb (the battery's 65 percent fuel) | 166.2 kt | 166.2 kt (the cap again), touchdown 153.7 kt, rollout 5,056 ft | the 135 kt flare scales to about 165 kt at that weight |
| Sustained turn, held speed, 400,000 lb: 250 kt at 15,000 ft | 34 degrees, 1.22 G | 60 degrees, 2.04 G | no figure; the real structural limit is 2.5 G at moderate weights |
| Sustained turn, held speed, full tank: 250 kt at 1,000 ft / 250 kt at 15,000 ft | 28 degrees (1.15 G) / none above 8 degrees | 54 degrees (1.72 G) / 24 degrees (1.07 G) | none found |
| Sustained turn, the same, at 300 to 400 kt and at 439 kt (the edge) | 54 to 60 degrees; 28 to 42 degrees | the same | none found |
| Instantaneous pull, 400,000 lb, 300 kt at 1,000 ft | 2.07 G | 2.07 G (G rows and loading unchanged) | structural limit 2.5 G (not cited here) |
| Roll rate (full stick) | 23.6 deg/s | unchanged | none found |

The Mach 0.7 probe's "no sustained turn above 20 degrees" at 15,000 ft is the edge:
439 kt is the record's top speed there. With the speed held it is 28 degrees at the full
tank and 42 at 400,000 lb, before and after.

Sources (all read 2026-11-15): Wikipedia, "Boeing B-52 Stratofortress", Specifications
(B-52H), through the migflug.com page that quotes them (max 565 kn at altitude, Mach
0.86; cruise 442 kn; ceiling 50,000 ft; rate of climb 6,270 ft/min; range 8,800 miles)
and the article text (service ceiling officially 50,000 ft, difficult to reach with a bomb
load; range 8,800 miles); ultimatespecs.com B-52H page (560 kt, cruise 442 kt, 6,270
ft/min, 50,000 ft, takeoff 9,843 ft, landing 6,562 ft); the Air Force B-52 fact sheet
(maximum takeoff 488,000 lb); the Jane's text in `B52.INF` (516 kt, 55,000 ft). The
ground-run and landing figures (8,000 ft at 488,000 lb, 4,900 ft from a 135 kt flare at
270,000 lb) are one post in the B-52 Stratofortress Association forum, which the fetch
tool could not open (HTTP 403); they were read from the search result's summary of it, so
they are the weakest figures here and are used only as a plausibility target, not as a
value to hit. No takeoff or approach speed was found in any primary source.

### Engine count (not changed)

`Configuration::from_source` clamps the record's `engines` to 1 to 4 and
`LiveConfiguration::validate` rejects more (`combat/live.rs`). What reads the clamped
count:

- `Engine::new` (`aircraft_systems/engine.rs`) clamps again and keeps a `shutdown` array
  of four and `thrust_shares` of four. The two engine-shutdown damage results (systems 9
  and 10, "Engine shutdown") each take 1 over the count of the power, so the B-52 loses
  25 percent a hit where the real jet would lose 12.5.
- `wreck::Power` (`wreck.rs`) keeps four per-engine accelerations; the yaw torque of a
  falling wreck spreads over the count.
- Checkpoints and replay: the live configuration record carries `engines`
  (`checkpoint_records.rs`), the wreck power array is in the live checkpoint and the
  golden fingerprint (`golden_tests.rs`).

What does not read it: fuel flow (the record's flow is the aircraft's total, scaled by
the throttle), sound (loops are per aircraft identity), the HUD and systems pages (they
show temperature, oil, hydraulics and total power, no per-engine rows) and the
contrails (the app reads the record's own 8, which is how the fallback spread past the
wing tips, below).

Honouring eight would mean widening the three four-element arrays to eight, allowing
1 to 8 in `live.rs`, and then re-pinning every aircraft's golden fingerprints and
checkpoint records, because the fingerprints walk the whole array (four entries become
eight for every aircraft) and the wreck power travels in the checkpoint. A guard that
leaves the other aircraft unchanged would need a variable-length array in a type that is
`Copy` and compared exactly. That is not a small, safe change, so it was not made. Option
for John: keep four (the cost is the 25 percent engine-out step), or schedule the
widening as its own slice with a simulation version bump.

### Ground alignment and contrails

Ground alignment: 0.4 a second, the transports' value (the fighters' 0.7 was the
BMB-A1 default). Fitted, as the transports' is.

Contrails: `contrail_offsets` (`tore-app/src/aircraft.rs`) now returns a fitted set for
the B-52's eight engines, in feet (lateral, up, aft): two at each of four pods, the
pods' centre lines 35.0 ft (inner) and 58.2 ft (outer) either side, from the drawn pods
(`B52.SH` at 2/3 ft a unit: inlet faces 15 units wide, aft faces 11 units, centres 52.5
and 87.4 units out; aft faces at y 18 and -8 units, so the points start 2 ft behind them:
10.0 and -7.3 ft; heights -0.7 and -1.7 ft). The engines sit 1.8 ft either side of the
pod centre. The real pods are about 35 ft and 58 ft out (B52-3). The old fallback gave
lateral points to +/-1.05 half-spans (97 ft against the 92.7 ft half-span). One test
(`the_b52_draws_eight_contrails_two_behind_each_pod_inside_the_wing_tips`) pins the set.

### Battery

`flight.py`: `b52` joins `VARIETY_AIRCRAFT`, `LIFTOFF_AIRCRAFT` (liftoff, retail-stall
and approach scenarios) and `HEAVY_AIRCRAFT` (the `gcurve` scenario, with a 1.15 G floor for the B-52 because its 2 G row over the 1.64 loading divisor is 1.22 G, `HEAVY_GCURVE_FLOOR`), with fitted windows
(liftoff 150 to 175 kt, approach 150 to 170 kt, recorded 158.6 and 166.2), the internal
fuel table (312,197 lb), a takeoff tick limit of 9,000 (the run takes 7,300 ticks; the
rest lift off inside 4,500) and a 12,000 ft runway for the liftoff and approach scenarios
(UKR airport 1 is 5,532 ft, shorter than the takeoff run). `main.rs`: `--flight-fuel`
accepts up to 400,000 lb (was 100,000, which the 65 percent landing weight exceeds) and
the scripted landing is now built after the fuel is set, so every aircraft's approach
flies the weight the scenario names (the fighters' differences are a few knots; their
recorded windows still pass, see the results in the baseline).

### Open for John

- The drag shape is a per-aircraft model change (`DragShape`), small and guarded, but a
  new shared concept. The alternative was to leave the 2,600 nautical mile range and the
  2,100 ft/min climb and report them, as M2K-8 did for the Mirage 2000 climb.
- The top speed (560 kt real, 515 kt record) and ceiling (50,000 real, 55,000 record) are
  reported only, as asked.
- The takeoff and landing run fits rest on one unofficial forum post. Say if the 4.8 and
  2.6 ft/s squared terms should wait for a better source.
- Engine count: four or eight (above).
- The record's 30 degree a second roll limit (the AC-130 family block) gives 23.6 degrees
  a second; no real figure was found.

## B-2 rig (B2-3, 2026-11-15)

Implementation, slices B2-3 and B2-4 run together (bomber batch A), Claude Sonnet
(sonnet-high). Binding: John's accepted decision 20 (2026-11-15): rig the elevon
wedges as whole panels (rule 12), drive the signed drag-rudder word from yaw, add
a fitted both-sides speed brake, rig the gear and the interim bay pose. The B-2
now loads through its own rig, `crates/tore-app/src/b2_animation.rs` (the shared
`variety_animation` row keeps only the layout, scale and `supported`), with its own
probe module (`aircraft_animation_probe/b2.rs`) and battery entries. Nothing in the
simulation changed. Frames are local only, in `.local/m3-aircraft/frames/B2-3/`.

Provenance: the face lists, hinge edges, retail open poses and gear plates are
spec-derived (retail `B2.SH`, read at load and refused if they differ). Everything
that moves them (limits, mixing, the speed brake, hinge heights, retraction
direction, the bay drop) is **fitted**, agent decisions of 2026-11-15, labelled
below. No retail bytes are committed.

### Elevons (rule 11 fold check and rule 12 mixing)

One four-face wedge per side with no state word (`4037 404e 4065 407a` right,
`40ce 40e5 40fc 4111` left). Re-checked by exact coordinates: no vertex of either
wedge is shared with any other face (7 distinct vertices per side, 0 neighbours).

| Face | Vertices | Move | On the hinge line | Fixed off the line |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `4037` top-of-wedge quad (right) | 4 | 4 | 0 (the line is the mid-thickness of the leading edge) | 0 |
| `404e` quad | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| `4065`, `407a` inboard triangles | 3 each | 3 each | 0 | 0 |
| Left `40ce 40e5 40fc 4111` | 4, 4, 3, 3 | all | 0 | 0 |

The whole wedge turns as one rigid body about its leading-edge mid-line (right
(63, -70, -3) to (120, -22, -3), left (-121, -22, -3) to (-64, -70, -3) in shape
units, a third of a foot each). The two leading-edge vertices at each end (z 0 and
-6) sit 3 units off the line, so the hinge-line opening against the fixed skin ahead
is at most 6 sin(angle/2) units: 0.9 units (0.30 ft) at pure pitch, 0.6 units
(0.20 ft) at pure roll and 1.5 units (0.49 ft) at the clamp. The probe measures the
midpoint of each leading-edge pair staying on the line (largest move 1.6e-7 ft) and
the wedge rigid to 5e-6 ft.

Mixing, rule 12: angle (positive lowers the trailing edge) = -0.30 x pitch
-/+ 0.20 x roll, right sign minus, left plus, clamped to +-0.50 rad. A pull raises
both trailing edges; a positive aileron raises the right and lowers the left. The
limits are the fleet's own fitted values (Mirage 2000, Rafale, MiG-31: 0.30 pitch,
0.20 roll), 17.2 and 11.5 degrees, 28.6 degrees at the clamp. **Fitted; no cited
B-2 elevon limit was found** (the one source found only says the outer elevons are
the primary pitch and roll surfaces and the inner ones low-speed, Virginia Tech
slides, `archive.aoe.vt.edu/mason/Mason_f/B2Spr09.pdf`; the mesh has one strip per
side, so the single wedge takes both terms). The flap lever moves nothing: the
flying wing has no flap panel.

### Drag rudders (word 6498) and the speed brake

The rig never sets word 6498 (a magnitude of 2 or more removes a pair and adds
nothing, B2-2). Each side keeps its two closed quads (`465f` upper, `4679` lower
right; `4600`, `461a` left) and turns each as one rigid plate about its own hinge
edge (z 0 for the upper plate, z -7 for the lower): right (177, -46) to (215, -71),
left (-178, -46) to (-218, -72). The open angle is read at load from the retail
open pose (the free edge's midpoint, about the hinge line), so the fully open rig
reaches the source pose to within 0.6 unit (0.2 ft), the plate's own chord stretch (the retail open
plate is 12.8 units on its chord against 12.1 to 12.4 closed, 5 percent, because the
source open pose is not an exact rotation):

| Plate | Hinge z | Angle to the retail open pose | Free edge z, closed to open |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Right upper | 0 | 47.6 degrees up | -3 to +6.4 and +7.0 (retail +7) |
| Right lower | -7 | 52.1 degrees down | -3 to -13.5 and -14.2 (retail -14) |
| Left upper | 0 | 50.3 degrees up | -3 to +7.0 and +7.2 (retail +7 and +8) |
| Left lower | -7 | 52.9 degrees down | -3 to -14.0 and -13.8 (retail -14) |

A closed quad has one winding, so the rig adds a reversed-winding twin (built on
the retail `back` face of the open pose: `47f5 47c1 46ea 471e`) while a side is
open, plus the retail vertical front plate and inboard cap (`480f 4829`, left `4738
4752`), drawn only while that side is open. Rule 11: each plate is a whole four
vertex quad, both hinge vertices on the hinge line (largest hinge move 1.6e-7 ft),
the two plates of a side meet only at the trailing edge, which opens by design.

**Mapping (fitted).** Open fraction of the right side = min(1, brake +
max(rudder, 0)); left = min(1, brake + max(-rudder, 0)). A positive rudder (a right
yaw) opens the right drag rudder and a negative rudder the left, each from closed
to the one open pose in proportion to the command. The real B-2 yaws by opening the
drag rudder on the side it yaws toward, which raises the drag on that wing (Aviationist,
"B-2 control surfaces" close-up of the pre-flight check, 2021-03-10; AeroXplorer,
"How does a B-2 Spirit fly without a tail?"; the flight computer blends them with
differential thrust). This is the same sense as the rig's `+1` (right), the repository's
positive rudder (trailing edge to starboard, yaw right). Probe rows
(`yaw-brake-combinations.csv`, 25 poses): the open sides match the formula, every
plate rigid, direction correct, the right free edge never falls as the brake
grows.

**Speed brake (fitted, decision 20; label fitted).** The shape encodes one side
open at a time (a signed word), so the both-sides pose cannot come from the word.
The rig opens both sides by turning the closed quads, so the pose is the same
geometry the left and right poses already use, mirrored and shown together: the
"compose both open poses" method works because the rig turns plates instead of
choosing a word. It is wired to the existing airbrake control (the `B` key,
`Switch::Airbrake`, `State::brake`, which ramps over the record's deployment time)
and its drag is the existing one (`airBrakesDrag` 256 in `B2.PT`, applied as
`airbrake x brake` by the flight model; the B-2 record is the B-1B's, so the figure is
the template's). Nothing was added to the simulation. With the brake at 1 both
sides are fully open whatever the yaw; at a part brake the yaw side opens further,
so the yaw stays visible below full. Cited use: the same surfaces open together as
air brakes (one source says they open symmetrically at low speed and on takeoff and
landing); that is a weaker citation than the yaw use, hence fitted.

### Gear (word 648c, +14 faces)

Seven plates, both windings each, retracting with the shared gear fraction
(angle = 90 degrees x (1 - gear), hidden at 0, the source pose at 1, so the
timing is the sim's own ramp). All hinge lines are fitted (the shape has none) and
every piece turns as one rigid body:

| Piece | Faces | Hinge (shape units) | Stow |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Main door leaves | `438d 43a4`, `449e 44b5` | line along Y at z -10 (2 units above the leaf's top edge at -12), at x -71 and 69 | inboard, flat inside the closed well |
| Main wheel plates | `441b 443a`, `452c 454b` | line along Y at z -9, at x -65 and 62 | inboard, flat inside the closed well |
| Nose front leaf | `4153 416a` | lateral line (0, 71, -9), its top edge | aft, flat above the belly |
| Nose rear leaf | `41ae 41c5` | lateral line (0, 97, -5), its top edge | aft |
| Nose strut and wheel plate | `4597 45b6` | lateral line (0, 96, -5), its forward top corner; steers about a vertical line through (0, 92) | aft |

The mains' hinge is raised above the leaf's top edge because the belly well panel
is at z -12 (`3cc9`): a plate hinged on its own top edge would stow coplanar with
that skin. Raised, the stowed plates lie at z -10 and -9, inside the closed well.
Direction (inboard mains, aft nose) is fitted, as the Mirage 2000 and the Tornado (no
B-2 gear retraction direction was found in public sources). Probe (`dense-gear.csv`,
202 values plus the near-stow sample): rigid at every value, never below the gear-down
pose, grounded at gear 1 at exactly 33 units (11.0 ft, the inner main plates), every
piece at or above its own hinge height near stow, main plates inboard of their gear-down
x, the strut foot aft of its gear-down y, 203 lines, all passing.

**Wheel brakes.** None exist in the shape (plates only, no wheels, no brake
word) and the simulation has no separate wheel-brake visual for any aircraft, so
"brakes" here is the airbrake and speed brake above.

**Nose wheel (decision for John's information).** The nose strut's lowest point is
33 minus 31 = 2 units (0.67 ft) above the inner main plates', and the simulation
stands every aircraft on one clearance below its model origin (the gear low point,
11.0 ft for the B-2) with the pitch held level on the runway (`start_on_runway`
sets pitch 0). So the B-2 sits level (0.00 degrees) with the nose wheel 0.67 ft
(8 inches) off the pavement; the geometry that would put it down is 1.39 degrees
nose down over the 27.7 ft wheelbase. **Chosen: accept it as the retail sit**, no
fitted nose contact point. Why: a nose point is not a rig change, it is new ground
physics (a per-aircraft contact table or a pitch on the ground) that the one-clearance
contact model does not have for any of the 48 aircraft, it would touch
`SIMULATION_VERSION` and determinism for a 1.4 degree effect, and the retail game drew
the same plates over the same clearance. The frames (`ground-*`) show the nose wheel at
or just off the pavement with no sinking and no visible float at normal distance.

### Bay (word 6486): interim

The four hanging plates (`4209 4220 4264 427b 431a 4331 42bf 42d6`, both
windings, x -27, -3, 1, 26, y -10 to 48, z -12 to -25) are added to the shape and drawn
only while `State::bay` is above 0, dropping from the belly line (z -12, their top edge
stays) to the full 13 units as the bay fraction goes 0 to 1 (fitted, interim). Nothing
raises the bay fraction for the B-2 yet: `State::bay_available` is true only for the
F-22, so in play the plates never appear, and `--flight-bay` refuses the B-2. B2-5
replaces this with real bay cuts, doors and the magazine grid (and owns the
`bay_available`, signature and release-timing change); the frames of the interim pose
(`bay-*`) came from a temporary, reverted patch to the capture option. The probe drives
`State::bay` directly (control `bay`, 5 poses).

Update (B2-5, 2026-11-15): the interim plates are no longer added or drawn; the fitted bay
doors, the belly cut and the lined recess replace them
([B-2 weapon bays](#b-2-weapon-bays-b2-5-2026-11-15)), `State::bay_available` is true for the
B-2 and `--flight-bay` accepts it. The probe's bay check and an 8-value bay sweep
(`bay-sweep.csv`) now test the doors.

### Burner, flame, hook, flaps

The B-2 has no flame word, no nozzle faces and no afterburner thrust (`engine_material`
returns no nozzle, `outlet_count` is 0, `--flight-devices` refuses a non-zero fifth
fraction). The probe marks `exhaust` and `flaps` not applicable and requires that they
move nothing; `hook` is not applicable (no hook). Nothing breaks: the exhaust and flap
levers leave the geometry identical.

### Probe result

`--animation-probe .local/m3-aircraft/checks/B2-3/probe`: `animation probe B2.PT:
268 neutral faces, 0 required/check failures` (B2-2: the same four required failures,
unmapped). Required controls now pass: elevator (the elevons, 5 poses), aileron (the
elevons, 5), rudder (the drag rudders, 5), gear (22), brake (the speed brake, 5) and
bay (5). `flaps` and `exhaust` are not applicable, accepted explicitly (the flying wing
has no flaps and no burner), `hook` not applicable. Grids: `pitch-roll-combinations.csv`
(25 poses), `yaw-brake-combinations.csv` (25 poses), `dense-gear.csv` (202 values): all
pass, rigidity at most 5e-6 ft, hinge gap at most 1.6e-7 ft. Battery entry:
`flight-animation-b2` (expects the three CSVs).

Frames (`.local/m3-aircraft/frames/B2-3/`, png with ppm; `cap.sh` and `batch1.sh` to
`batch4.sh` record the commands; chase view, 200 kt, paused pose): `elevon-{neutral,
pitch-up,pitch-down,roll-right,roll-left}-{rear3q,rear,side}` and 3x crops
`crop3x-elevon-*-rear3q`; `drag-{neutral,yaw-left,yaw-right,speed-brake}-{rear3q,
rear,side}` and `crop3x-drag-*-rear3q`; `gear-{down,up,mid}-{under,side}`,
`gear-mid-{0.25,0.75}-under`; `bay-{open,half}-under`, `bay-open-gear-down-under`;
`ground-{side,nose-side,front3q,rear3q,side-low,front-low}` (a runway start, gear
down, level). Looks: the open drag rudder reads as a dark upper plate and a lighter
lower plate hinged off the trailing edge on the yaw side, both open together for the
brake; the elevon wedge leans visibly at pitch down and at roll; the gear folds
whole and inboard, hidden at 0.

## B-2 sensors, HUD and cockpit (B2-7, 2026-11-15)

Slice B2-7 (implementation mode, bomber batch A) made the B-2's retail cockpit family
work. It applies John's accepted decisions of 2026-11-15: **17**, use `B2.HUD` and the
`~B2*` art (opinionated), and **18**, keep the B-1B's five sensor rows with no pod body
drawn (the Tornado precedent). The earlier B-2 sections stay as written (B11): the
[source review](#b-2-source-review-2026-11-15) described the HUD field as empty and
the eye point as the fixed seat, and BMB-A1 left the glass failing closed and the
eye shared. This section records what the game now does. Changed: the B-2 glass
polygon (`hud_aperture.rs`), a per-aircraft pilot's eye table (`mirrors.rs`, with the
call sites that pass the aircraft type), and two tests (`hud_aperture.rs`, and the
retail-reading `crates/tore-import/tests/b2_cockpit.rs`). Nothing else in the
simulation changed. Frames are under `.local/m3-aircraft/frames/B2-7/`, logs under
`.local/m3-aircraft/checks/B2-7/`.

### Bindings (spec-derived names, opinionated binding)

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Record `hudName` | null pointer (as retail; TORE never reads it) |
| `AircraftId::hud()` | `B2.HUD`, which names the instrument frame `~b2_p`, read by `Hud::parse` as `~B2_P.PIC` (81 x 80) |
| Cockpit stem, shape stem | `B2`, `B2` |
| Forward art | `~B2H.PIC`, **1394 x 508** (not the 1280 x 490 of the older families, so the glass aperture is keyed to this size) |
| Other pictures of the family | `~B2.PIC` (581 x 214) and `~B2S.PIC` (1737 x 633): the same picture at the other two resolutions, which TORE does not read (as for every family) |
| Overlays | none: `~B2_LH.PIC`, `~B2_CH.PIC` and `~B2_RH.PIC` do not exist, so the B-2 is a no-overlay stem (BMB-A1) |
| Sensor rows (fixed) | `VIS340.SEE`, `F18R.SEE`, `F18.ECM`, `PAVESPK.SEE`, `AV8IR.SEE` |

The family is four pictures in `FA_1.LIB` (`~B2.PIC`, `~B2H.PIC`, `~B2S.PIC`,
`~B2_P.PIC`) and `B2.HUD` in `FA_2.LIB`. No other flyable identity uses the stem or the
HUD (the retail `AURORA.PT` and `TU160.PT` name `b2.HUD`, and neither is on the roster).
The new test pins all of it, and the record's `viewOffset` (0, 30, 60).

Views: front (the art with the HUD in its glass and the six small-layout windows), look
left and right 45 degrees (the art turns away with the look; with no overlay stem nothing
takes its place, as for the F-16 and the AC-130), 90 degrees and 60 degrees up (open
sky, no art), `--flight-view 3` (F2 Back, from the pilot's eye, below) and `--flight-view
4` (F3 Up, which does not use the eye). There is no down view. The instrument windows
draw with the `~B2_P.PIC` bezel; the ten pages (0 to 9) draw (frame
`instrument-pages-0-to-9`).

### The glass aperture (fitted, measured)

`~B2H.PIC` has no combiner glass: it is the open cockpit window of a large aircraft,
like the AC-130's picture that the B-52 flies. Its transparent pixels are three
separate panes, divided by the left diagonal strut and the right strut: the **main
window** (x 141 to 1021, y 91 to 455, 247,572 pixels), a left side pane (x 0 to 322,
y 90 to 440, 67,994 pixels) and a right side pane (x 1087 to 1393, y 91 to 418, 83,066
pixels). `hud_aperture::mask` had failed closed for the B-2 (BMB-A1's interim, an empty
mask, so no HUD drew). It now has a 20-vertex polygon along the main window's boundary,
a pixel outside it: the top beam's lower edge at y 90, the right strut's funnel down
to the monitor housing (x 1006 to 1021), the sloping console top (y 420 at x 540, 456
at x 300 and left) and the left strut, from (140, 456) to (398, 90). The opaque art trims
it, so the mask is exactly the transparent pixels inside: 246,986 pixels, 99.76 percent
of the main window, no opaque pixel, none in either side pane, one connected region. The
HUD symbols sit in the middle of the main window in the frames, well inside the polygon;
the side panes would matter only to symbols far off axis, and a decision to draw the HUD
there too (the whole-picture AC-130 choice) is a one-line change if John wants it. Two
tests pin it: a synthetic one (centre in; above the beam, both side panes and the console
out; an opaque pixel inside left out; any other picture size fails closed, and the F-117's
mask is still empty) and a retail-reading one (the same three panes by flood fill, the
exact coverage, no opaque pixel, no side pane, connected, at least 98 percent).

### How the HUD fits a bomber

`B2.HUD` is a resource of the B-1B and AURORA family (`TU160.PT` names it too), but TORE
reads from any HUD module only the primary colour, the instrument frame name and the
three window text colours (`tore-formats::hud`); the symbols are the one shared
drawn HUD. So the B-2's HUD is the same drawn HUD as every aircraft's, and what changes
for a bomber is what it is offered:

- It draws flight data (heading tape, speed and altitude boxes, flight path marker,
  pitch ladder), the weapon and its count (`31 MK-82`, `4 GBU-27`), `NO TARGET` with
  no designation, and the **bomb sights**: the level-bombing cue for the Mk 82 rows (`LVL`),
  and for the Paveway rows the laser box with `IN RNG`/`REL` and `LSR`, `TTI` and the
  seeker (frame `hud-slot3-gbu27-laser-sightpin`: `REL 0:14`, `LSR 4.5`, the box on the
  pinned point; without a pin the laser row reads `NO LASER`).
- It has no air-to-air weapons, so no lock circle or gun cue appears (the record has no
  gun and no missile). The radar and IR contacts show in the radar window, not as a HUD
  lock.
- The status column on the right of the glass shows `GEAR`, `BRAKE` (the speed brake,
  which opens both drag rudders), `FLAP` and `HOOK` as they apply (frame
  `hud-gear-down-brake` reads `GEAR` and `BRAKE`). `BAY` shows only while a bay is open
  and the aircraft is the F-22 (`State::bay_available`), so it does not show for the
  B-2 yet; B2-5 owns the bay and its cue.

### The eye point (fitted; a per-aircraft table now exists)

The B2-2 finding stands: the shared seat (7 ft up, 10 ft ahead of the origin, shape y 30
and z 21) is 10 to 17 ft behind the B-2's glass, under the spine skin. No per-aircraft
eye existed (`mirrors::pilot_eye` was one fixed offset), so B2-7 adds the smallest table
that leaves every other aircraft unchanged: `mirrors::eye_offset(Option<AircraftId>)`,
(up, forward) in feet, with the shared 7 and 10 for every identity and an unknown type,
and one entry, **the B-2: 10 ft up and 20 ft ahead**. It is fitted and labelled so.

Measured on the neutral `B2.SH` (1/3 ft a unit): the centre-line top surface rises from
z 20.7 (6.9 ft) at y 20 to the spine peak of z 23.8 (7.9 ft) at y 44 (14.7 ft ahead),
falls to 22.0 at y 60 (20 ft), where a steep face drops into the glass cavity, and the
windscreen runs from z 21 at y 64 (21.3 ft) to z 13.7 at y 80 (26.7 ft), then the nose
slope down to z 6.5 at y 88. The seat is at the windscreen's start, 2.7 ft above the
roof (z 22 at y 60), so F2 Back looks over the roof and the spine, not out of the
inside of the skin. A seat inside the skin (6 ft up) was drawn and rejected: Back shows
the inside faces of the spine as a grey blur (frame `f2-back-eye-inside-skin-rejected`).
The record's `viewOffset` (0, 30, 60), which no host code reads, gives the same
figure read at the shape's 1/3 ft a unit (30 up, 60 ahead = 10 ft, 20 ft); that
reading of the field's units is unproven and is not used by the code.

What reads the eye, and what changed (all pass the aircraft type now; none of it moves
for another aircraft):

| Reader | Takes the table |
| --- | --- |
| F2 Back in flight (`aircraft.rs`, own aircraft) | yes |
| F2 Back from another recorded or live aircraft (`flight_views.rs`: `Body` carries the type from its pose) | yes |
| Replay: the cockpit camera (`director.rs`), the HUD camera (`views.rs`) and the listening seat (`viewer.rs`) | yes, so the replay's Back view and its sound sit where flight's do |
| The mirror rear feed (`mirrors::camera`) | no: it stays on the shared seat. Only cockpit families with mirror seeds draw it, and `B2` has none (`--cockpit-sheet` prints `b2 NO MIRRORS FITTED`) |
| The forward cockpit (2D art), the look and zoom controls, the chase and fly-by views, F3 Up, the external camera | no: they never used the eye (the forward view looks from the origin) |
| Padlock and the target camera | no: they do not read the eye |

Tests: `mirrors::tests::only_the_b2_has_its_own_pilot_eye` (the table for every
identity), `flight_views::tests::back_from_a_b2_sits_at_its_own_seat`, and the existing
replay Back test now compares against the typed eye. Every other aircraft's Back eye is
unchanged (the replay and flight view tests pass). The mirror feed for the other
aircraft is untouched.

### Sensors (decision 18: kept as retail, no pod body)

`--sensor-summary` reads: `B2: radar F18R.SEE search 90 nmi 60x60 deg track 50 nmi
45x45 deg look-down 0 ADVANCED; infrared AV8IR.SEE search 15 nmi 60x60 deg track 15 nmi
45x45 deg; visual VIS340.SEE search 10 nmi 170x140 deg track 5 nmi 170x140 deg; jammer
F18.ECM LATE strength 0.30; signature radar 1 infrared 15`.

- **No pod body draws.** `PAVESPK.SEE` and `AV8IR.SEE` are fixed rows at (0, 0, 0)
  with flag `0x1008`, not stations, so no store pose is built for them (the Tornado
  precedent). The external frames show the wing undersides and the nose bare
  (`external-threequarter`, `external-side`, `external-front-under`, `external-under`).
- **The laser designator works through the fixed Pave Spike row.** With the GBU-27 row
  selected and `--combat-command sight-pin` the HUD reads `LSR 4.5`, `REL 0:14` and the
  target camera `PIN`, `ZOOM 3`, `LASE` with the range `4.5 NM` (frame
  `target-cam-gbu27-laser`). Without a designation the HUD reads `NO LASER`.
- **The target camera** (page 4) opens in the small layout (`SLEW`, `ZOOM 3`) and shows
  the pinned point when designating.
- **The IR view.** `--sensor-channel ir` puts the radar window on the `AV8IR.SEE`
  channel: `IR`, 10 nmi, with the target's contact (frame `ir-view-channel-ir-radar-page`).
- **The radar is the F-18's `F18R.SEE`, not the B-2's APQ-181**, kept as the record says.
  The modes it gives a bomber are the shared **air-to-air** ones: RWS search (to 90
  nmi) and TWS with a fire-control track (to 50 nmi), both in the scope at 5, 10, 25, 50,
  100 and 150, plus the IR channel (M cycles them, Y toggles history). There is **no
  air-to-ground mapping mode** in the shared radar (`docs/radar.md`: air-to-ground
  radar awaits ground weapons), so the B-2's strike work is the targeting sight and
  the laser, which the fixed Pave Spike row provides. Frame `radar-mfd-livefire-track`
  reads `TWS 10 ... TRACK`.
- **The RCS page shows the stealth signature.** Page 0 reads `SIG 1` with the exposure
  contour a dot at the centre of the 50 nmi scope, against `SIG 154` and an oval for
  an F/A-18 in the same capture (frames `rcs-page-b2-sig1-crop3x` and
  `rcs-page-f18-sig100-crop3x-comparison`; the F-18's record says 100 and the page
  shows the figure with its aspect and loaded stores). The record's radar signature of 1 and infrared 15 are as
  retail; the RWR and the stealth model are not in this slice.

## B-2 flight review (B2-8, 2026-11-15)

Validation and fitting, slice B2-8 (bomber batch A), Claude Sonnet (sonnet-high).
The B-2 flies the hybrid adapter's `variety` configuration built from `B2.PT` and
`B2.SH` with BMB-A2's real thrust (69,200 lbf), weights (empty 158,000 lb, fuel
167,000 lb, maximum takeoff 376,000 lb) and the 6 lb/s fuel flow kept (John has not
answered the 7 lb/s question). The question was whether the bomber flight-tuning block
(the B-1B's, 160 of 208 statements, B2-0) makes the B-2 too slow. Raw probe output is
local: `.local/m3-aircraft/checks/B2-8/` (`before/`, `after/`, `run_perf.sh`,
`run_probes.sh`, `battery.txt`).

### The cause

**The slow figures were mostly the probe's climb schedule, not the tuning.** The
BMB-A2 probe climbs at "max(450 kt, Mach 0.8)" true. The hybrid adapter's drag is not
a polar: parasite drag is the full thrust times the square of the speed over the 1 G
fast edge (`State::airframe_drag`: reference thrust x lapse x (V / top speed)^2, plus
the G-pull, flap, gear and airbrake terms). The B-2's own 1 G edge at sea level is
750 ft/s (444 kt, Mach 0.67), so at 450 kt the drag is already more than the thrust
and the aircraft cannot climb there at all. The BMB-A2 numbers (5,000 ft in 1,000 s,
11,479 ft highest in 1,500 s) are a bomber held 6 kt above its own top speed. The
same aircraft on a bomber's schedule (full thrust, constant 250 kt equivalent airspeed
to Mach 0.70, pitch held by a speed integrator, the new `PROBE_CLIMB=250,0.70`) climbs
5,000 ft in 94 s (3,190 ft/min average) and 40,000 ft in 1,098 s (18.3 min), at the
record's thrust and weight, with nothing changed. Real figure: an initial climb of
3,000 ft/min (aerospaceweb "B-2 data"; Aerocorner repeats it). Thrust to weight at the
real normal takeoff weight (336,500 lb) is 69,200 / 336,500 = 0.206, the published
0.205 (Wikipedia, "Northrop Grumman B-2 Spirit").

**What the B-1B terms do and do not do.** Checked one by one against a flying wing of
172 ft span and about 5,140 square feet (Wikipedia; aerospaceweb gives 5,000):

| Term (B2.PT, the B-1B's value) | What it does here | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `coefDrag` 256, `loadedDrag` 0 | `coefDrag` is read only by the native diagnostic; the hybrid drag is scaled from the thrust and the 1 G edge, and `loadedDrag` 0 adds nothing | no effect on the flight; kept |
| `_gpullDrag` 12 (induced drag) | drag per G above 1 is weight x 12 / 256 = 0.047 W. A lifting-line estimate for a span of 172 ft, area 5,140 square feet and e 0.95 gives 0.036 W per G at 300 kt at sea level and 0.063 W per G at Mach 0.8 and 40,000 ft | inside the band; kept |
| `flapsDrag` 38, `flapsLift` 51 | the flap lever is a generic high-lift device for every aircraft (stall x 0.75, lift and drag): the flying wing has none drawn (B2-3) but keeps the lever like the Mirage F1 and the F-117 | fleet-level, not touched |
| `airBrakesDrag` 256 | weight x 1.0 x brake x speed share: a fighter airbrake, 0.44 G of extra deceleration at 312 kt on a 325,000 lb flying wing | **fitted to 64** (below) |
| `rudderDrag` 128, `bayDrag` 25, `wheelBrakesDrag` 12 | read by the native diagnostic only, not by the hybrid step | no effect |
| swing-wing or sweep terms | none exist in the flight model for any aircraft (the Tornado review found the same, TOR-8) | nothing to remove |
| `loadedElevator` 40 | divides the G limit by 1 + 0.4 x (fuel + stores) / empty weight: +3 G becomes 1.95 G at 325,000 lb, 2.0 G at the default load | kept (the real G limit was not found) |

**Takeoff and landing speeds** come from the envelope's 130 kt sea-level 1 G stall edge,
which the model scales by the square root of the weight over the empty weight
(`stall_reference_fraction` is 1 for every variety aircraft): at the 373,000 lb default
load that is a flapped stall of 150 kt. That is physically sound for this wing (a
wing-loading estimate for 373,000 lb, about 72.6 lb per square foot at a lift
coefficient near 0.9, gives about 154 kt), so no lift fit was made.

### What was fitted

1. **Ceiling 49,000 to 50,000 ft (opinionated, the figure is real).**
   `maxAlt` and the top vertex of the 1 G and 0 G polygons move up 1,000 ft
   (`B2_CEILING_FT`, a `CORRECTIONS` row and a `fit_envelopes` arm, the F-117's way).
   Cited: the game's own Jane's text `B2.INF` ("Service ceiling: 15,240 m (50,000 ft)"),
   Wikipedia "Northrop Grumman B-2 Spirit" (specifications), aerospaceweb "B-2 data",
   Air Force fact sheets (all read 2026-11-15). Nothing else in the polygons moves. The
   practical effect is small: level flight held to 48,000 ft (414 kt) before and after,
   and the scripted climb tops out 100 ft higher (48,160 to 48,263 ft), because the band
   between the two edges is narrow in the last thousand feet.
2. **Speed brake, `airBrakesDrag` 256 to 64 (fitted).** See below. A `CORRECTIONS`
   row, applied only while the record still holds 256 and the rest of the B-2 rows are
   retail.
3. **Nothing else.** Top speed, climb, acceleration, turns, thrust lapse, stall and
   lift were left as the record and the shared model give them; the figures below show
   why.

### Before, after and real

Probe: `performance_probe` (clean unless said; 325,000 lb at full fuel; normal takeoff
336,500 lb is `PROBE_PAYLOAD=11500`, maximum 376,000 lb is `51000`), ground probes at
`--theater UKR --ground-start 1` with the default load (gross 373,000 lb: 48,000 lb of
bay stores and the full tank). "Before" is the repository at 1e162bac.

Sources read 2026-11-15: Wikipedia "Northrop Grumman B-2 Spirit" (specifications, Block
30; Migflug copies it), aerospaceweb.org "B-2 data", Aerocorner "Northrop Grumman B-2
Spirit", the Air Force and Air Force Global Strike Command fact sheets, the National
Interest "How Fast Is the B-2 Spirit Stealth Bomber?", and the game's own Jane's text
`B2.INF` (retail media, not committed). The published top speed is not settled: the
record's Mach 0.84 to 0.87 sits between the two published figures (Mach 0.80 and Mach
0.95) and is 5 percent above aerospaceweb at both altitudes (421 kt and 460 kt against
444 kt and 483 kt), so it was **not changed**; see the question at the end.

### The speed brake and the drag rudders

The brake is the existing airbrake control (the `B` key, `State::brake`), which opens
both drag rudders in the rig (B2-3), and its drag is `weight x airBrakesDrag / 256 x
brake x the speed share`. The yaw use (one rudder opens with the pedals) has no drag
term in the flight model: only the brake position does, and the sim's rudder does not
add drag on the hybrid adapter (`rudderDrag` is read by the native diagnostic only).
Idle throttle, level, ten seconds, `PROBE_ONLY=brake` (extra deceleration of the brake
over the clean run, G):

| Altitude, speed | Template 256 | Fitted 64 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1,000 ft, 223 kt (0.5 of the edge) | 0.22 | 0.08 |
| 1,000 ft, 312 kt (0.7) | 0.44 | 0.14 |
| 1,000 ft, 401 kt (0.9) | 0.63 | 0.20 |
| 20,000 ft, 332 kt / 427 kt | 0.47 / 0.67 | 0.15 / 0.20 |
| 36,000 ft, 348 kt / 448 kt | 0.42 / 0.70 | 0.15 / 0.21 |

The template's brake slowed the 325,000 lb flying wing by 100 kt in ten seconds at 312
kt, a fighter's airbrake. The fit sizes the brake from the drawn plates: two plates a
side (upper and lower), each about 15.2 ft along the hinge by 4.1 ft of chord and
opened about 50 degrees, so about 190 square feet of frontal plate for all four, at a
drag coefficient of 0.8 in a thick wing's wake: q S Cd over the weight is 0.14 G at 300
kt and 0.25 G at 400 kt at sea level. The model's speed share is 0.66 at 300 kt and
0.93 at 400 kt, so the factor that fits both is 0.22 to 0.27 of the template; 64 is a
quarter. **Fitted; no public drag-rudder drag exists.** The model's brake drag cannot
fall with altitude as the real dynamic pressure does, so at 36,000 ft it is about
three times the plate estimate. The landing rollout, flown with the brake out, is 19
percent longer (2,330 ft against 1,960 ft); the 5,532 ft runway still has 853 ft left.
At approach speeds (about 150 kt) the brake adds under 0.05 G. The wheel brakes
(`Tuning::brake_deceleration` 18 ft/s^2, shared by every variety aircraft) were not
touched; the rollout is still shorter than the 3,450 ft published.

### Other findings

- Air maneuvers (`--headless-flight`, same ticks as the Tornado set): level 7,200
  ticks, pull 7,200 (2.1 G, loop completed), loop, sprint 36,000 ticks (450.4 kt), rudder, devices (3 s deployments), stall-recover and
  spin-recover (entered at tick 3, recovered at 1,252 after 0.98 revolutions) all
  ended with `non_finite=0` and no crash; `dive` and `overspeed` ended in the overspeed
  loss by design. `after/probes/` and `before/probes/` match except `devices` (the
  lighter brake: 216.7 kt against 232.1 kt) and the landing rollout.
- The full-stick pull is 2.1 G at 330 kt and 1.41 G at 461 kt and above (the +3 G row
  divided by the loaded-elevator rule), and 0.70 G of push.
- The gear limiting speed in Jane's text (224 kt) has no counterpart in the flight
  model; not checked or added.
- Fuel: 6 lb/s gives 464 minutes at military power and 5,486 nm at the trimmed
  cruise. At the cited 7 lb/s it would be 5,000 nm. Unchanged, for John.
- The probe: `performance_probe` gained `PROBE_CLIMB=KEAS,MACH` (the bomber climb),
  `PROBE_ONLY=brake` and `PROBE_TURN_MACH`; `flight.py` adds `b2` to the variety,
  liftoff, retail-stall and approach scenarios (windows 140 to 165 kt and 140 to 170
  kt, fitted, agent decisions; recorded 158.1 and 166.2 kt), with a longer takeoff
  allowance (10,000 ticks) and the approach fuel capped at the probe's 100,000 lb
  (`--flight-fuel`).

Session log; the new tests are `the_b52_b2_and_f117_read_their_real_figures_only_while_retail`
(extended: ceiling, brake, polygons, stealth signature) and
`the_b2_climbs_at_a_bombers_rate_and_its_speed_brake_is_a_modest_one`), `--headless-flight
1200 --aircraft b2` (303.2 kt level at 5,010 ft, no crash, 0 non-finite), `battery.py
--scenario '*-b2' --lane flight` 6 of 6 (animation, liftoff, liftoff-retail, approach,
variety, skin), `check_docs`.

Provenance: the thrust, weights and fuel are BMB-A2's (John's decision 16, real); the
ceiling is opinionated (the real figure, an agent decision); the speed brake factor and
the battery windows are fitted (agent decisions 2026-11-15); the real figures are
public pages and the game's own Jane's text, for comparison only; nothing else changed.

Open for John: (1) the top speed: keep the record's Mach 0.84 to 0.87 (inside the
published Mach 0.80 to 0.95), or trim the 1 G fast edge to Wikipedia's Mach 0.95 at
40,000 ft (about +14 percent at 40,000 ft, the F-117's one-vertex way); (2) the fuel
flow, 6 or the cited 7 lb/s; (3) whether the wheel brakes and rollout (shorter than the
published 3,450 ft) should be fitted for the bombers (a per-aircraft tuning change);
(4) whether the drag rudders should add yaw drag on the hybrid adapter (`rudderDrag`
128 is unread there).

## F-117 weapon bays (F117-5, 2026-11-15)

Opinionated (John, 2026-11-15, decision 25: "cut two fitted belly bays, two doors
each"); every number below is **fitted**, agent-authored, from the measurements in
the [stores specification](../spec/stores-on-pylons.md#f-117-weapon-bays-f117-5-2026-11-15).
**The door count is fitted** (two a bay, four in all): the real count was not found in
any public source. Earlier sections stay as written. This replaces the interim open pose
of [F-117 rig (F117-3)](#f-117-rig-f117-3-2026-11-15) and settles the proposal in
[F-117 hardpoints and the bay](#f-117-hardpoints-and-the-bay-for-john).

**Stations.** Rows 4 and 5 (location 3, flags `0x1100`, one store of weight class 20)
are re-placed by `placed_on` as fitted `Location::Magazine` stations, through the new
table `tore_sim::combat::bays::STATIONS` (the F-22's three rows moved into it with their
values unchanged). Mounts, feet right / floor / forward: left -3.0 / -2.78 / 0.0, right
+3.0 / -2.78 / 0.0. F117-2 had scaled the rows to +/-2.55 ft; a GBU-27's fins span 5.4 ft,
so two stores 5.1 ft apart would cross fin tips, and the mounts move out to 3.0 ft. The
"floor" is the height of the lowest fin tip (the magazine rule hangs the axis half the fin
span above it): the axis is 1.0 ft above the belly plane, and the fins hang 1.7 ft below
it, between the open doors.

**Geometry (feet right / forward / up from the reference point).**

| Part | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Belly plane | -1.478 (the shape's z -5 units after the height factor) |
| Openings | right x 0.2 to 5.8, left x -5.8 to -0.2; 5.6 ft wide, 18.0 ft long (-9.0 to +9.0 forward); a 0.4 ft keel between them |
| Doors | two a bay, 2.8 ft wide, hinged at the inner and outer edges, 90 degrees down; open they hang to -4.28 |
| Recess | roof at +0.822 (2.3 ft deep), four lined walls and a ceiling in the shape's own wall grey, drawn only while the doors are off their seat |
| Trapeze rail | 0.4 ft wide, 0.6 ft deep under the ceiling on each bay's centre line, -5.5 to +3.5 forward |
| Belly skins cut | `34e6`, `2f0a`, `2f1d`, `2f5d`, `2f8e`, `3076` (together they cover both openings exactly; nothing else overlaps them) |

The shape's own open pose (word `4c56`: two wall plates and the swapped belly triangle) is
no longer drawn; one of its wall plates is the material of the lining, and its painted
trapeze art did not line up with the bay centres (it sits about 0.8 ft off the keel), so it
is not used. The cut-out is closed on every side: the lining is a box (ceiling and four
walls) under an intact top skin, the recess is 2.3 ft under a skin at least 2.4 ft above
the belly everywhere over the openings (the forward outer corner is the limit), so nothing
opens to the sky (frames below).

**Drawing.** The shared helper `crates/tore-app/src/bay_doors.rs` (belly doors from
`roster_animation::cut_doors`, the lined recess and the rail) is driven by one row of
`bays::OPENINGS`; `f117_animation.rs` names the six belly skins and the lining's addresses
(`0x7000` and up). `variety_animation` routes `faces()` to the F-117 rig. The B-2 and B-52
add a row to `STATIONS`, a row to `OPENINGS` and their own face lists.

**What each bay admits.** The two rows admit the same 23 stores, one a bay (the audit's F-117
line is 46 placements, was 38): the retail mask `0x1100` takes 19 (`PAVEWA3` as the row's
default, `GBU29`, `GBU29P`, `GBU30`, `GBU38`, `MK82`, `MK82HD`, `MK82P3`, `MK84`, `CBU87`,
`CBU89`, `MK20`, `RBK250`, `RBK500`, `FAB250`, `FAB500`, `AGM88`, `AGM45`, `AT2`), and
`aircraft_stations::extra_weapon` adds four Paveway II laser bombs the mask leaves out:
`GBU10`, `GBU10A`, `PAVEWAY` (GBU-10 class) and `GBU12`. `GBU16` is refused by name (the
audit's donor rule needs it stated; the real jet's laser bombs are GBU-10, 12 and 27).
`GBU28` (4,500 lb), the multi-store packs and the stores heavier than weight class 20 stay
out by the row. No BLU-109 or GBU-31 record exists (the `GBU29` and `GBU30` records are the
JDAM class). The default is two `PAVEWA3` (GBU-27), 4,000 lb of the real 5,000 lb load
class. The retail mask admits the AGM-88, AGM-45 and AT-2, which the real jet does not
carry; they stay because they are retail data and fit (listed for John).

**Clearances in feet, doors open** (`TORE_STORES_PREVIEW_BAYCLEAR=1`; positive is clear,
negative is how far the drawn store reaches into the part). Default GBU-27, both bays:

| Part | Gap |
| --- | ---: |
| Inner and outer door planes (fin tips at x 0.3 and 5.7 against planes 0.2 and 5.8) | 0.10 |
| Bay aft end / forward end | 1.06 / 3.04 |
| Trapeze rail (body top under the rail) | 0.10 |
| The other bay's store (nearest vertices) | 0.60 |
| Recess roof (upper tail fin tips) | -1.40 |
| Fuselage top skin (upper tail fin tips, 0.62 ft through it at x +/-5.7, 7.9 ft aft) | -0.62 |
| Below the belly plane (lower fin tips, inside the 2.8 ft doors) | 1.70 |

The GBU-27 clears both doors, both ends, the rail and its neighbour. **It does not fit
inside the fuselage**: its tail fins are 5.4 ft across in a fuselage 3.3 to 4.1 ft thick, so
the four upper tail fin tips stand 1.4 ft above the recess roof and 0.62 ft above the
top skin at their aft ends (about 0.6 ft of fin tip through the dorsal skin, seen only from
above while the doors are open). The retail fins are drawn larger than real
(`store_sizes.rs`); this is the one clip left, for John (options in the stores
specification). During the 1 s door swing the leaves also pass the lower fin tips.
Alternatives (the two rows' other stores, minimum of the two door planes, the ends and the
skin): GBU-27 family and GBU-10 family clear the doors (0.10 and 0.89 ft) and the ends (GBU-10
0.16 ft forward); the GBU-10 reaches 0.57 ft above the roof and clears the skin; the GBU-12
clears the doors by 1.25 ft and the roof by 0.28 ft; the AGM-88 and AGM-45 stand 0.13 ft
past the forward end (inside the 0.3 ft rule); every other store clears all parts, by at
least 1.85 ft at the doors and 2.10 ft at the roof. Full table:
`.local/m3-aircraft/checks/F117-5/matrix.txt`.

**Bay door timing.** The F-22's: `State::bay` travels in 1.00 s (reversible); a bay
release asks for the doors, the weapon leaves once they are at 0.95 (tick 116 after the
press, 0.958 in the actual one-press probe), the doors stay 1 s after the release and close
1 s later. `bay_available()` is now true for every aircraft with a row in `bays::STATIONS`
(the F-22 family and the F-117; the B-2 and B-52 on their rows); the open-bay signature term
reads `State::bay` on the RCS page only (no change to a row a radar reads), so it now applies
to the F-117 at 1.5 times with the doors fully open, and the F-22's values are unchanged.
Update to [F117-3 bay (interim)](#bay-interim-f117-4-f117-5-replaces-it): replaced.

## F-117 ordnance, sensors and cockpit (F117-6/7, 2026-11-15)

Slices F117-6 (ordnance, default load, countermeasures) and F117-7 (sensors, HUD, cockpit,
instruments) ran together (implementation mode, bomber batch A). They apply John's accepted
decisions of 2026-11-15: **3** (switch the retail night rule on with the import), **25**
(default two GBU-27 in the bays; F117-5 cut them), **26** (keep `PAVESPK.SEE` relabelled as
the IRADS turret, keep `AV8IR.SEE` as the FLIR, drop the jammer row; BMB-A2 dropped it) and
**28** (`F117.HUD` and the F117 cockpit art). Earlier F-117 sections stay as written (B11);
they carry Update lines that point here. Frames are under
`.local/m3-aircraft/frames/F117-6/`, logs under `.local/m3-aircraft/checks/F117-6/`.

### F117-6: the load, the bays and the sights

**Default load (unchanged by this slice, checked).** Rows 4 and 5, the two bay stations (F117-5),
each hold one `PAVEWA3` (GBU-27) by default: 4,000 lb of stores, 52,000 of the 52,500 lb maximum
with the 18,500 lb of fuel. Rows 0 to 3 are the fixed equipment rows (`VIS340.SEE`,
`PAVESPK.SEE`, the cleared `F18.ECM` row, `AV8IR.SEE`): they are not stations, hold no
weapon, and the Load Ordnance page shows only the two bays (frames `load-ordnance`,
`load-ordnance-laser`; the four lower frames of the right-hand panel are empty by design, there
is nothing to put in them). `--validate-ordnance` reads `F117.PT: 2 source rows, 0 optional weapon
rows, 46 compatible weapon placements, 0 tank placements; defaults and restart passed; catalog 23
normal, 83 Cheat`, and the whole audit passes (48 aircraft, 20 recovered stations, 4,784 weapon
placements, 233 tank placements, 80 pod placements, 240 Cheat-only; no pin moved).

**What the page offers.** Each bay admits the same 23 stores, one a bay (F117-5: the retail mask
`0x1100`'s 19 plus the four Paveway II laser bombs `GBU10`, `GBU10A`, `PAVEWAY` and `GBU12`). The
air-to-surface page lists them over three screens: the page's first screen with the laser bombs
and the cluster and Russian bombs is the frame `load-ordnance-laser`. **There are no presets**:
Load Ordnance has no named loads for any aircraft, so the default load (two GBU-27) is the only
one, and a bay takes one store from the list at a time (the Tornado and F-15E slices had none
either). The retail mask also admits the AGM-88, AGM-45 and AT-2, which the real F-117 does not carry
(F117-5 listed them for John; unchanged here).

**Live fire, the target camera and the laser all work from the bays.**
- `--live-fire --aircraft f117 --weapon-slot 1` releases the left bay's GBU-27 (one shot, ammo
  `[0, 1]`, payload 4,000 to 2,000 lb) once the doors are open; with `--flight-bay 1` it leaves at
  once. The HUD reads `ARM`, `1 GBU-27`, the reach scale (`R 4.6`, `4.9`, `1.0`) and the new `BAY` cue
  while the bay is available (frame `target-cam-irads-gbu27-laser`).
- Designation and the laser run through the fixed `PAVESPK.SEE` row, as the F-16C's and the B-2's: with
  `--combat-command sight-pin` the target camera reads `PIN`, `ZOOM 3`, then `LASE` (it blinks twice a
  second, so a frame at the wrong phase misses it) with `4.7 NM`, and the HUD reads `IN RNG` and
  `LSR 4.7`. A hand-off with the laser key (`laze`) reads `NO LASER` and `LSR RDY` (frame
  `hud-slot1-gbu27-no-laser-laze-off`).
- The scripted run (new battery scenario `a2g-laser-f117`, `--a2g-run UKR QUCOL --attack laser --aircraft
  f117 --load PAVEWA3 --station 0 --count 1`, 15,000 ft at 480 kt): designated at 8.0 s (`laser Lasing`),
  released from the left bay at 16.2 s inside the reach (`in-reach yes`, mode `Guiding`, spot owner 0),
  tracked to the tank, which is destroyed (`hp 0/200`), as the F-15E's belly Paveway does. (A count of 2
  on the one station is refused: with the other bay's bomb it is over the take-off limit.)

**Countermeasures: none, as decided.** BMB-A2 cleared the `F18.ECM` default row (no source was found
that the real F-117 carried dispensers). Nothing shows: the Weapons window reads `2 GBU-27` with no
`CHAFF` or `FLARE` line (the window's `no_countermeasures` rule, which TOR-13 wrote for the Tornado IDS
(Clean), keys on the record's counts), the RWR never lights `JAM` (`no_jammer`: there is no
jammer row), and the systems page shows engine, fuel and no countermeasures. Pressing the chaff and
flare commands and `--jammer-on` with `--countermeasure-preview 60` changes nothing and breaks nothing
(frame `countermeasure-keys-no-dispenser-strip`, no panic in the log). `--sensor-summary` reads `jammer
none`.

### F117-7: sensors

**Sensor rows.** `VIS340.SEE`, `PAVESPK.SEE` and `AV8IR.SEE`: `--sensor-summary` reads `F117: radar none;
infrared AV8IR.SEE search 15 nmi 60x60 deg track 15 nmi 45x45 deg; visual VIS340.SEE search 10 nmi
170x140 deg track 5 nmi 170x140 deg; jammer none; signature radar 1 infrared 20`. The records, the sight
and the channel behave as the shared ones; decision 26 is text only.

**Labels (text only, nothing else changed).** One new table entry, `AircraftId::sensor_names()` (`SensorNames
{ sight: "IRADS", infrared: "FLIR" }`, `None` for every other aircraft, the B-2 included), and four readers:

| Where | Every other aircraft | The F-117 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Window 4's title (`instruments.rs`, `CombatReadout::sight_title`) | `TARGET CAM` | `IRADS`; a weapon's seeker picture (and its lost feed) keeps `TARGET CAM`, as it is the weapon's view |
| Load Ordnance sensor line (`ordnance::sensor_helper`) | `Built-in laser designator: no pod needed for laser ordnance.` or `Aircraft laser pod equipped` | `Built-in IRADS: no pod needed for laser ordnance.` (the shared hemisphere-gimbal rule would have said `Aircraft laser pod equipped`) |
| Radar window, infrared channel (`combat_view.rs`) | `IR` | `FLIR` (frame `crop-flir-irads-radar-page`: `FLIR`, `10`, the contact) |
| Replay Sensor View's sight name (`replay/viewer/views.rs::sight_record`) | the sensor record's own name (`PAVE SPIKE`, `AAS-38`) | `IRADS` for the laser row, `FLIR` for the infrared row |

Everything else says what the shared code says: the HUD's `LSR`, `IN RNG`, `ARM`, the page's `PIN`, `ZOOM`,
`LASE`, the keys. `--sensor-summary`'s record names and the logs keep the retail file names. Tests:
`aircraft::tests::only_the_f117_has_its_own_sensor_names`, `instruments::tests::the_target_page_title_is_the_aircraft_sight_name_when_it_has_one`
and the extension of `ordnance::tests::the_helper_line_says_what_the_aircraft_brings_from_its_data`.

**Radar: none, as the record says.** The radar window reads `NOT INSTALLED` (frame
`cockpit-front-view`), the channel key still reaches the infrared channel (the FLIR above), and nothing in
the sim, the data link or the AI assumes a radar for the F-117 (`has_radar` is false, BMB-A1's datalink
test lists it as the eighth type without one; `radar()` is `None`). **No ground-mapping mode**
exists in the shared radar, as for the B-2 (a sensor change, John's call).

**RCS page: `SIG 1`, and the open bay raises it.** Page 0 reads `SIG 1` with a dot for the exposure contour
with the doors closed and `SIG 2` with the bay open (frames `rcs-page-closed`, `rcs-page-bay-open`; the
second frame has released its GBU-27, which the stores term does not count against, since the
real figure the page rounds is 1 x 1.5). Against a 90 nmi radar nose-on that is 9.0 nmi closed and
11.0 nmi open (F117-0, F117-5; the page prints the rounded figure). Nothing in the signature code changed.

### F117-7: the cockpit

**Bindings (spec-derived names, opinionated, decision 28).**

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Record `hudName` | null pointer (as retail; never read) |
| `AircraftId::hud()` | `F117.HUD`, naming the instrument frame `~f117_p`, read as `~F117_P.PIC` |
| Cockpit stem, shape stem | `F117`, `F117` |
| Forward art | `~F117H.PIC`, **1673 x 508** (wider than the B-2's 1394 x 508 and the 1280 x 490 of the older families, so the aperture is keyed to this size) |
| Other pictures | `~F117.PIC` and `~F117S.PIC` (the other two resolutions, which TORE does not read) |
| Overlays | none: `~F117_LH.PIC`, `~F117_CH.PIC` and `~F117_RH.PIC` do not exist, so the F-117 is a no-overlay stem (BMB-A1) |
| Record `viewOffset` | 0, 20, 60 (the Tornado's, no host code reads it) |

All of it is pinned by the retail-reading test `crates/tore-import/tests/f117_cockpit.rs` (the three sensor
rows, `radar()` none, the names, the HUD module and its panel frame, the four-picture family, the art size,
no other aircraft on the family, `viewOffset`).

**The glass aperture (fitted, measured).** `~F117H.PIC` has no combiner. Its transparent pixels are four
panes: a left pane (x 5 to 572, y 21 to 480, 189,456 pixels) and a right pane (x 1100 to 1667, 189,970
pixels), the open sky strip above the bar (x 735 to 940, above y 118), and the **windscreen** between the
two bow posts, under a thin bar: x 712 to 962, y 129 to 366, **56,572 pixels** (a flood fill from the
middle). The console's vent block and two teeth break its lower edge from y 346. `hud_aperture::mask` had
failed closed for the F-117 (BMB-A1's interim). It now has a 16-vertex polygon one pixel outside the
windscreen (the bar's lower edge at y 128, the posts' inner edges widening from x 725 and 949 at y 141 to
x 712 and 962 at y 224 and back in to x 714 and 960 from y 308, the foot at y 367 for the opaque console to
trim). It covers **56,562 of the 56,572 pixels** (99.98 percent): no opaque pixel, no other pane, one
connected region. Two tests pin it: a synthetic one (centre and the lower corner in; the sky strip, both
panes and the foot out; an opaque pixel inside left out; any other picture size, the B-2's included, fails
closed) and a retail-reading one (the same four panes by flood fill, the exact coverage, no opaque pixel, no
other pane, connected, at least 98 percent). The HUD is the windscreen's, narrow (250 pixels wide), and the
symbols sit well inside it (frame `cockpit-front-view`); drawing it in the side panes too would be a
polygon change.

**Views.** Front (the art with the HUD in its glass and the six small-layout windows, bezel
`~F117_P.PIC`), look left and right 45 degrees (the art turns away with the look; nothing replaces it, as for
the B-2, F-16 and AC-130), look up 60 degrees (open sky), F2 Back from the pilot's eye (below) and F3 Up (does
not use the eye). The ten instrument pages (0 to 9) draw with the F-117 bezel (frame `instrument-pages-0-to-9`,
a headless panel snapshot, so its window 4 reads the generic title: the labels are a combat-readout feature).
No mirror seeds exist for the family, so no mirror draws (`--cockpit-sheet` prints `NO MIRRORS FITTED`; the
rear feed stays on the shared seat for every aircraft).

**The eye (fitted, from the scaled shape).** `mirrors::eye_offset` gains the F-117: **6 ft up and 14 ft
ahead** of the model origin (the shared seat is 7 up and 10 ahead; the B-2 is 10 and 20). Measured on `F117.SH`
after F117-2's per-axis real-size factors (x 0.7647, y 1.0463, z 0.8869, 1/3 ft a unit): the centre line top
surface rises evenly from the tail (0 ft at about 26 ft aft of the origin, 3.9 ft at 9 ft ahead), then the
faceted canopy runs from 10.5 to 18.8 ft ahead with its crown 4.6 ft up at 14.6 ft ahead (4.4 ft at 12 ft,
3.6 ft at 17.4 ft, 2.9 ft at the base of the windscreen at 18.8 ft). The seat is the middle of the canopy, 14
ft ahead, and 1.4 ft over the crown, so F2 Back looks over the glass and down the spine to the ruddervators
(frame `cockpit-view-back-f2`; the shared seat's frame is `pre-view-back-f2-shared-eye`, 4 ft too far aft of the
cockpit). The record's `viewOffset` (0, 20, 60), read at the shape's 1/3 ft a unit, would put the eye 6.7 ft up
and 20 ft ahead, at the front of the glass; that reading of its units is unproven and is not used. Every other
aircraft keeps the shared seat: the test `mirrors::tests::only_the_b2_and_the_f117_have_their_own_pilot_eye`
(the renamed B2-7 test) checks the table for every identity. Readers are the ones B2-7 listed (F2 Back, replay
Back, cockpit and HUD cameras and the listening seat); the forward cockpit, the padlock and the target
camera never read the eye.

### F117-6: the night rule is live (decision 3)

The retail rule, in `tore-formats/src/quick_template/tables.rs` (`NIGHT_STEALTH_AIRCRAFT` `F117.PT` and `B2.PT`,
`NIGHT_AAA` `ZSU23.NT`, `NIGHT_AAA_SKILL` 0), was written as dormant because neither aircraft was flyable.
The matching code (`tore_world::surface::resolve::night_stealth`) compares each friendly wing's
`AircraftId::pt()`, so it woke by itself when BMB-A1 added the identities. This slice made it deliberate:
the stale "dormant" comments are corrected, the old "dormant today" assertion in
`surface::tests::the_night_rule_mans_every_aaa_slot_with_a_novice_zsu23` is replaced, and one new test
(`the_night_rule_wakes_for_a_friendly_f117_or_b2_at_night`) pins the condition for both aircraft: night
only (clear by day stays off); any of friendly wings 1 to 3 with planes in it (a wing of zero planes does
not count, an enemy wing never does); and that the creator's AAA strength carries it into both
`GroundTarget::from_spec` (a template's `<aaa>` slots) and `AreaDefense::from_spec` (the enemy's gun sites).
**It applies to the B-2 the same way.** No data, behaviour or digest changed for a mission with another
aircraft or by day. See [surface defenses](../spec/surface-defenses.md#templates-and-defended-slots).
A wing the lobby fills per plane (`plane_aircraft`) is not read, as retail's rule keys on the wings.

Provenance: sensor rows, HUD module, panel names, cockpit art and the night rule spec-derived (retail); the

## F-117 flight review (F117-8, 2026-11-15)

Validation and fitting, slice F117-8 (bomber batch A), Claude Sonnet (sonnet-high). The
F-117A flies the hybrid adapter's `variety` configuration built from `F117.PT` and
`F117.SH` with BMB-A2's corrections (maximum take-off 52,500 lb, ceiling 45,000 ft, the
1 G fast edge at 36,000 ft trimmed to Mach 0.92). The record's own thrust (21,600 lbf,
two non-afterburning F404-F1D2), empty weight (29,500 lb), tank (18,500 lb), flow (2
lb/s), G rows (-3 to +6), 180 degree a second roll block and the other envelope rows
were read and validated, not changed. Raw probe output is local:
`.local/m3-aircraft/checks/F117-8/` (`before/`, `after/`, `run_perf.sh`,
`run_probes.sh`, `battery.txt`, `headless-f117-1200.txt`). "Before" is the repository at
c10543c7, "after" is with the one fit below.

### What is wrong

**One thing was clearly wrong and citable: the speed brake.** The record carries
`airBrakesDrag` 256, a fighter's airbrake, and the hybrid adapter turns it into a drag of
weight x 256/256 x the brake x the speed share: 0.30 G of extra deceleration at 295 kt,
0.49 G at 413 kt and 0.66 G at 530 kt at 1,000 ft on the 48,000 lb jet (more than the
whole clean drag). The real jet has none: a pilot's account says "there are no drag
devices on the jet: no speed brakes, no flaps, nothing" except the landing gear and, on
landing, the drag chute (jetcareers.com forum, "F-117 Cloaking Device", read 2026-11-15,
an unofficial source; the post also says aerodynamic braking was prohibited). The shape
has no airbrake word to draw (F117-3, "Brake: none ... the real jet has none"), and the
record's `flapsLift` and `flapsDrag` are already 0, so the record agreed about the flaps
and disagreed about the brake. **Fitted:** `airBrakesDrag` 256 to 0
(`F117_AIRBRAKE_DRAG`, a `CORRECTIONS` row applied only while the record still holds 256
and the other F-117 corrections hold). The brake lever still moves the state but adds no drag. A visible effect: the
scripted landing deploys the brake on its rollout, so the rollout from touchdown goes
from 2,504 ft to 3,117 ft (default load) and from 2,569 ft to 3,218 ft (clean), nearer
the published figure, and the `devices` probe's final speed is 435 kt against 372 kt.

**Nothing else was clearly wrong.** Each remaining difference is either inside the
published scatter, rests on a source too weak to fit to, or is a shared-model feature:

- **Top speed.** The record's sea-level edge, 592.2 kt (Mach 0.90), equals the Wikipedia
  infobox's 594 kn (684 mph); the high-altitude edge is Mach 0.92 after BMB-A2, the
  published Mach. The other published figures disagree: 541 kn "at high altitude"
  (Wikipedia body text), 562 kt (flugzeuginfo.net), 646 mph or 656 mph, Mach 0.98
  (Aerocorner, MILAVIA), 594 kn. A lifting-line style check says a 21,600 lbf jet with a
  zero-lift drag coefficient of 0.025 to 0.03 on 780 square feet would be thrust limited
  at 520 to 570 kt at sea level, so 592 kt is at the top of the plausible band (it needs
  a coefficient of 0.023), but no source gives sea-level speed alone, so it was **not
  changed**; see the question at the end.
- **Climb.** The published rates do not agree (2,820 ft/min in the Wikipedia body, 3,000
  ft/min and 9,000 ft/min on two other listings; not one states a weight or altitude).
  The model gives 6,800 ft/min over the first 5,000 ft and 9,300 ft/min at its best (clean,
  full tank, 300 KEAS to Mach 0.75). At a thrust to weight of 0.45 and a drag of about
  0.2 of the weight at 370 kt, 6,000 to 9,000 ft/min is what the arithmetic gives, and
  2,820 ft/min cannot be a maximum. No fit.
- **Drag shape.** A per-aircraft `DragShape` (the B-52H's way, B52-8) was **not
  justified.** The B-52's edge is a placard; the F-117's is thrust limited with no
  afterburner (the real jet cannot go supersonic), so the shared square law
  (drag equals the thrust at the edge) is the right kind of curve. The one published
  figure that checks cruise drag, the range, points the other way from the B-52's: the
  model's range at Mach 0.82 and 36,000 ft is 1,516 nautical miles against the published
  930 (Wikipedia, flugzeuginfo; 1,140 with a full bomb load, Aerocorner), so the model's
  cruise is more efficient than the real jet, and a drag shape that lowers cruise drag
  would widen the gap. The fuel flow, not the drag, is the likelier cause (below).
- **Takeoff and landing speeds.** The model's weight-scaled stall puts the default load's
  rotation at 169.7 kt and liftoff at 177.2 kt (3,647 ft run), clean 162.8 and 170.3 kt
  (3,091 ft), against a published rotation speed of 160 kt and takeoff speed of 165 kt
  (a FlightGear simulator guide and an unnamed listing: unofficial, no weight), so the
  model is 6 to 8 percent high on weak figures. The `--retail-stall-speeds` figure,
  146.5 kt, is 11 percent low against the same figures, so the real number sits between
  the two switches. The approach is 166.2 kt (the cap, 0.85 times the record's 195.5 kt
  landing limit) with touchdown at 170 kt at a 45,525 lb landing weight: Aerocorner says 150
  kt approach and the FlightGear guide 150 to 160 kt touchdown at AoA 9 degrees, but the
  pilot account says the jet is Approach Category E (166 kt or more), "oftentimes the
  approach speed was in the 180s". With the 150 kt published at an unstated and probably
  lighter weight (the speed scales with the square root of the weight: 166 kt at 45,525 lb is 150 kt at about
  37,000 lb, a plausible landing weight, 29,500 empty plus 7,500 of fuel), the model agrees. No fit; the battery
  windows are loose.
- **Takeoff and landing distances.** The takeoff run is 3,647 ft against the published
  6,200 ft take-off distance and the landing 3,117 ft against 7,400 ft (Aerocorner; neither
  states a weight, a surface or whether it is a ground run or a distance over a 50 ft
  obstacle). The shared takeoff has no flap, gear or induced drag and no thrust lost with
  speed, a physical ground-run estimate (T/W 0.41, 278 ft/s liftoff, 0.33 g mean) is about 3,600 ft,
  and the real jet lands with its **drag chute**, which the model does not have
  (see below), so these are not fitted.
- **Thrust lapse.** The shared lapse (`exp(-h/70,000)`) keeps 0.60 of the sea-level thrust
  at 36,000 ft; the B-52 fit used 0.3 for a TF33. No F404 figure was found, so unlike the B-52
  (TF33, B52-8) it was not fitted. Of the model's figures this is the one most likely to
  make the F-117's 4,000 to 4,600 ft/min climb rate at 30,000 to 35,000 ft too good.
